what: judo.sh generate-root failed with a Maven daemon connect timeout because the mvnd registry file was corrupt.
why: Corrupt ~/.m2/mvnd/registry/1.0.2/registry.bin (Bad string size). Local tooling state, not a catalog topic.
workaround: Killed mvnd processes, deleted registry.bin, reran generate-root.

what: generate-root stopped with 'manual changes in generated files' on .gitignore after the generated project was copied into the existing repo.
why: The builder copied the generator output over the repo's tracked .gitignore, so the generator saw a hand edit. The catalog does not say how to adopt generated files into a repo that already has its own .gitignore.
workaround: Restored the generated .gitignore, added .pi/dashboard/kb/ to .git/info/exclude, reran generate-root (exit 0).

what: Ran create-judo-project in /tmp/gen and copied the output into ~/Projects/webshop-test.
why: The target folder already held FUNCTIONS.md and git history. The catalog does not say whether create-judo-project may run in a non-empty repo or which folder to use.
workaround: cp -a of /tmp/gen into the repo, then merged .gitignore by hand.

what: The catalog gives the create-judo-project goal and its parameters but not the plugin groupId or version. The builder took version 1.0.0.20260311 from ~/.m2, which then pulled template 1.0.0.20261109 from judo-ng.
why: Build-process section lists parameters only. Plugin coordinates and a version pin are not documented, so the builder guessed from the local Maven cache.
workaround: Used the locally cached plugin version found under ~/.m2/repository/hu/blackbelt/judo.

what: The CLI doc says the judo-cli.jar is downloaded by ./judo.sh build. In this generated project, generate-root did not create target/judo-cli.jar. Running mvn -DgenerateRoot validate did.
why: The catalog describes the download as part of judo.sh build. The generated root pom has its own download-cli profile that runs on generateRoot, so the catalog is incomplete for the new-project case.
workaround: Ran mvn -B -DgenerateRoot validate, which copied target/judo-cli.jar.

what: Guessed the ESM type name Namespace in a query and got an error.
why: Type name was not checked against the metamodel before the query. Minor.
workaround: Queried the real types (Model, Package, StringType, NumericType) instead.

what: Mapping a TransferObjectType to an entity made the CLI auto-create members, forms, tables and views. The builder's hand-added DataMembers then failed validate --strict with binding and uniqueness errors.
why: The catalog does not say that a mapped TransferObjectType creates its members and UI scaffolds, so the builder assumed it had to create them.
workaround: Discarded the unsaved edits and rebuilt the model without the hand-added MAPPED members.

what: ActorType create warned that realm does not apply, because the actor was effectively anonymous.
why: The builder left anonymous unset while setting a realm. The accesspoint doc says realm applies only when the actor is not anonymous.
workaround: Second update set realm, managed=false and kind on webshop::Shop; the warning went away.

what: managed=true on an actor principal is meant to insert the principal row at first login, but the runtime does not do this. An AuthenticationInterceptor is needed.
why: The advanced-modeling pattern doc warns that auto-insert is not implemented in the current runtime, and the JIT best-practice confirms it.
workaround: Builder set managed=false and planned the row differently (see c01-11 and c01-45).

what: A Keycloak user and the application's actor row are two separate stores. The runtime needs both before it can resolve the actor.
why: Stated by the builder in its seed script header. Matches the catalog's Keycloak Users and the Entity Store section.

what: No documented recipe for the first login user of a local dev app: no test user, no seed data and no credentials are given for the generated Keycloak realm.
why: Grep of agent-docs found only integration-test users and the test realm file. The local-development doc has no login step. The builder had to create a Keycloak user and a DB row by hand.
workaround: Created Keycloak user shop/shop through the admin REST API and inserted a t_webshop_shop_user row with psql. Wrapped in scripts/seed-dev-user.sh.

what: The builder improvised the first-user fix before searching the kb. Its final report said the catalog had no recipe, then the kb search found the JIT provisioning doc and the platform behaviour section.
why: The kb-first habit was not applied at the start. The catalog did cover the row side (AuthenticationInterceptor JIT), though not the Keycloak user side.
workaround: Recorded as GAPS 15a after the user asked for kb-first on problems.

what: local-development.md gives the app URL as http://localhost:8181/apps/. The app is at /webshop/Shop/, and /apps/ only lists bundles.
why: Doc is out of date for the generated app path.
workaround: Used http://localhost:8181/webshop/Shop/ (from the Karaf start log).

what: Keycloak on the local port is served under /auth (Keycloak 23 with a relative path). Root and /realms return 404, and the catalog gives http://localhost:8080 with no path.
why: judo.sh starts Keycloak with --http-relative-path /auth, which the local-development doc does not mention.
workaround: Used http://localhost:8280/auth for admin and realm calls.

what: Port 8080 was already in use by another project's container, so Keycloak failed to take the default port.
why: Local environment conflict. The catalog does document keycloak_port as an override.
workaround: Set keycloak_port=8280 in judo.properties instead of the -o start option.

what: The generated judo.properties sets dbtype=hsqldb, but local-development.md says the default run uses PostgreSQL in Docker.
why: Doc and generated default disagree.
workaround: Changed dbtype to postgresql in judo.properties.

what: The predefined Text type is limited to 250 characters, which is too short for a product description. The catalog does not say so and does not name a long-text type.
why: Type doc lists StringType widget properties but not the Text length limit.
workaround: Added StringType LongText with maxLength 4000 in webshop::types.

what: No model-level way to show a price with two decimals in the generated table. The table shows 89.9 and 129.5.
why: The generated table valueFormatter uses Intl.NumberFormat with defaults. formatValue exists in the model but the table column does not set fraction digits.
workaround: Patched the generated table component (see c01-21).

what: The table column customizer example in table-hooks.md uses a (original) => ... signature and registration that do not match the shipped type, which is () => ColumnCustomizer.
why: Docs out of date against utilities/table.ts in the generated app.
workaround: Not used. Builder edited generated code instead.

what: After the generated table was patched and listed in .generator-ignore, ./judo.sh build -f failed with 'manual changes' on many generated frontend files (App.tsx, auth files, components). Only build -f -i passed.
why: Generator checksum check is not satisfied by the module .generator-ignore entry, so every changed or unlisted generated file blocks the frontend build. -i disables the check and refreshes checksums, which also hides real manual edits.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh build -f -i, later ./judo.sh build -M -B -i.

what: Patched one generated table component to use min and max fraction digits of 2, and listed the file in the frontend module .generator-ignore.
why: No model-level or documented hook produced 2 decimals, and the builder judged a one-file patch the quickest path to S04.
workaround: Interim one-off fix; later orchestrator reverted it in Round 1.

what: Browser automation clicks and fills often did not reach the page. The builder then blamed slow app response and used many fixed waits and DOM eval clicks to move around.
why: Agent-browser tool problem. Refs went stale on re-render, text selectors failed, and clicks sent no events in several cases. Not an app latency issue.
workaround: Fixed waits (10 to 40 s), DOM eval clicks, direct location.hash changes, REST curl for data checks.

what: Creating a product through the browser form failed with 400 MISSING_REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTE, while the same create by REST succeeded.
why: Browser fill and keyboard input did not commit the numeric Price field (values were shown in the field but not in the React state). Evidence points to the tool, not the app.
workaround: Checked S03 with curl REST calls instead of the form.

what: Said the app was slow to respond (15 to 40 s per click). The orchestrator later showed the server answers in milliseconds.
why: Wrong diagnosis from unreliable browser clicks; no curl timing was done to check.
workaround: Kept the fixed waits.

what: kb_get returned 'not found' for paths that kb_search had just listed, so the builder could not read those docs.
why: Path resolution in the kb tool fails for some listed sections; index refresh was still running at the time.
workaround: Read search snippets, or grepped the catalog directly.

what: The kb read guard fired about 25 times with 'consecutive searches without consulting the knowledge base' while the builder read catalog files with bash and read.
why: Guard counts source reads as searches. It nagged on every bash call that touched the catalog.
workaround: Ignored; some turns then used kb_search.

what: Context-mode replaced long bash output with a search summary, so Maven and log output could not be read directly. The builder had to write output to files and read them.
why: Output summarising in ctx_search hid the lines the builder needed for the first Maven run.
workaround: Redirected output to /tmp/wsout files and read them with read.

what: kb_search results were fragmented and marked stale while the index was still refreshing.
why: Index refresh was running at the start of the session.
workaround: Re-ran searches later.

what: Builder read the catalog through bash grep, sed and read for most of the first hour, instead of kb_search and kb_get. This is why the kb call share was low.
why: No kb-first rule was in the first prompt (the user later added it at line 723).
workaround: User steering at L723 and L756 changed the habit.

what: Builder ran validate, curl, log reads and browser checks between build steps. The user then said to check only at the end and to use kb for every question.
why: Check-as-you-go habit; the first prompt asked only for a final check.
workaround: Accepted the user rule at L906 and L907 for later rounds.

what: Shell commands used on macOS: GNU 'timeout' is not installed, and a find / scan timed out after 60 s.
why: Builder assumed a Linux shell and ran a whole-disk find.
workaround: Dropped timeout and ran Maven directly.

what: Paths under /tmp failed in the read tool (ENOENT) because the path resolves to /private/tmp on macOS.
why: Tool path handling for the macOS /tmp symlink.
workaround: Read the /private/tmp path or used bash cat.

what: judo.sh stop did not stop the foreground judo.sh start process or Karaf. The builder killed the leftover processes by PID.
why: Start was run under nohup and stop only tears down the Docker services and not the Karaf child.
workaround: pkill on judo.sh start and console.out, then restart.

what: After a frontend-only rebuild, Karaf still served the old frontend bundle from application/.karaf/system. The builder had to delete application/.karaf and restart.
why: Unpacked Karaf assembly was not refreshed by build -f; the old jar stayed in .karaf/system.
workaround: rm -rf application/.karaf, then build -i and start.

what: Karaf log after a restart showed NoClassDefFoundError for EolExecutionContext in the RDBMS OSGi bundle.
why: Unknown; the builder saw it and did not pursue it. Login and data still worked.

what: The frontend uses a hash router. Pages open at /webshop/Shop/#/Shop/Products/..., so direct paths without the hash return 404. The catalog does not mention this.
why: Frontend docs do not describe the router type or the URL shape.
workaround: Used hash URLs (for example #/Shop/Products/AccessTablePage).

what: Karaf startup prints 'Visit http://localhost:8181/api-spec/webshop', but that URL returns 404.
why: Startup log link does not match the served API spec path (the REST root is under /api/).
workaround: Used REST paths from the generated frontend services.

what: The REST contract for updates and lists is not documented: the paths under /api/webshop/Shop/Shop/..., the X-Judo-SignedIdentifier and X-Judo-Mask headers, and the ~list and ~update verbs.
why: Builder had to read the generated frontend services to find the update path and headers.
workaround: Read ProductInfoServiceImpl.ts and headers.ts, then called REST with curl.

what: A stale view-page identifier from before a restart gave INVALID_IDENTIFIER (400) in the browser, and the console showed Axios errors.
why: Signed identifiers become invalid after a restart. The catalog covers this in the Identifier Signing and signed identifier sections.
workaround: Cleared localStorage and sessionStorage and went back to the list.

what: The generated table does not open the view page on a row click in a way the builder could find. The only row-click doc was the e2e test helper, and the embedded table row view button applies to references.
why: The catalog has no section on how a TransferObjectTable opens its view page (rowOperations versus row click).
workaround: Used a DOM eval to click the grid cell, which opened the view page.

what: Clicked Back on a view page opened directly by URL. Back did nothing, because the breadcrumb stack was empty.
why: Breadcrumb navigation records only in-app navigation. The builder expected browser history.
workaround: Re-ran the path list to view, then Back, which worked.

what: validate --strict failed with ExposedTransferObjectTableHasColumns (no columns on the viewable table). The fix was the fill command, which the builder found by trial.
why: The accesspoint doc states the rule, but the fill command is not in the judo-cli reference (openspec sweep item MO-172 lists it as missing).
workaround: fill webshop::ProductInfo --pages view,form,table.

what: Tried create -t MenuItemAccess, which the CLI rejects because MenuItemAccess is created automatically for an actor's access.
why: Builder tried the create command on an auto-generated element.
workaround: Used create -t Access on the actor and let the CLI create the menu access.

what: Build log showed ERROR lines for com.sun:tools systemPath ${tools.jar} but BUILD SUCCESS was reported.
why: Generated pom uses a relative system path for tools.jar. Noise, not a failure.

what: Modelled the shop login as EntityType ShopUser (username is identifier), a ShopUserInfo transfer object mapped to it, and ActorType Shop with principal ShopUserInfo and managed=false.
why: Managed auto-insert is not implemented in this runtime (advanced-modeling-patterns), so the principal row must come from elsewhere.

what: Price is a NumericType with precision 12 and scale 2. LongText is a StringType with maxLength 4000. Product has name, description and price members.
why: Price needs two decimals; the predefined Text type is too short for a description.

what: Set dbtype=postgresql and keycloak_port=8280 in judo.properties, and committed them.
why: Local-development says the default is PostgreSQL in Docker, and port 8080 was taken.

what: Wrote scripts/seed-dev-user.sh (idempotent Keycloak user shop/shop plus the ShopUser row) instead of building a JIT AuthenticationInterceptor, because the interceptor adds backend code beyond Level 0.
why: Level 0 scope. The JIT best practice explains the interceptor, but the builder judged it out of scope.

what: Checked S03 create and update with curl REST calls rather than the browser form.
why: Browser form did not commit numeric input (see c01-23). The later user rule asked for checks only at the end.

what: Project scaffolded from the ESM fullstack template, CLI jar obtained, shop frame model built, app built and started, login to the shop home page verified in the browser.
why: Level 0 frame.
workaround: Manual Keycloak user and ShopUser row (c01-11).

what: Product entity with name (String), description (LongText) and price (Price, NumericType scale 2). Product form shows Price, Name and Description.
why: S02 acceptance.

what: ProductInfo transfer object on the Shop access (createable, updateable). Create and update checked by REST: Running shoe 89.90 changed to 79.90, plus Trail backpack and Wool socks. Browser create not reliable.
why: S03 acceptance.
workaround: curl instead of UI (c01-23).

what: Product list (table) shows name and price. Price column shows two decimals after the generated table was patched and rebuilt.
why: S04 acceptance.
workaround: Patched generated table component (c01-21).

what: Product view and edit page shows name, price and multi-line description. Back verified only after in-app navigation (list, row, view, Back).
why: S05 acceptance. The builder's first Back check was invalid (page opened by URL).
workaround: DOM eval clicks and hash navigation (c01-22, c01-41).

what: Data persisted across ./judo.sh stop and start: products still listed after restart (Running shoe 79.9, Wool socks, Trail backpack).
why: S06 acceptance.
workaround: Needed manual process kill and rm -rf application/.karaf (c01-33, c01-34).

what: Builder assumed ./judo.sh generate would regenerate the frontend table component after reverting the S04 patch. It did not; the frontend build (judo.sh build -f -i) was needed.
why: Builder assumed the generate step covers frontend files; it only writes the scaffolds and model-derived sources.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh build -f -i, after which the table component was regenerated.

what: The kb says to re-fetch the judo-cli.jar with ./mvnw -f application/model/pom.xml -N validate, but the project has no mvnw wrapper. The command failed with exit 127.
why: Catalog gives a wrapper command that the generated project does not ship. Plain mvn also did not fetch the jar; the root-pom profile route (mvn -B -DgenerateRoot validate) worked.
workaround: Used mvn -B -DgenerateRoot validate to fetch target/judo-cli.jar.

what: ./judo.sh generate runs a clean that deletes target/judo-cli.jar. Every model edit made through the CLI jar after a generate fails with 'Unable to access jarfile'.
why: Generate wipes the target folder, and the jar lives there. The required order (fetch jar, change model, save, then generate and build) is not documented as a single sequence.
workaround: Re-fetched the jar before each model change and ran generate and build after the model was saved.

what: Setting customImplementation=true on the ProductInfo_Table price element makes the generated table component use useTrackService without importing it. The frontend build fails with TS2304 'Cannot find name useTrackService'.
why: Generator bug in the table component template for custom-implementation columns. The build recovery section (delete generated src folders and rebuild) did not fix it.
workaround: Set customImplementation=false on the table price element, regenerated, and built. The price column is handled by the column customizer hook instead.

what: For the shared price component the only registration point the kb documents is the generated src/custom/application-customizer.tsx. The builder asked the user before editing that generated file and adding it to .generator-ignore, which the quality bar forbids without asking. The user approved.
why: The quality bar forbids editing generated files; the kb documents no other registration place for custom visual elements.
workaround: User approved the exception; to be logged in GAPS.md.

what: Builder read that a custom visual element is a model-flagged extension point: set customImplementation on the element, then register an FC under CUSTOM_VISUAL_ELEMENT_INTERFACE_KEY with the per-element key from the container's customization.ts. The kb says there is no generic CUSTOM_COMPONENT_HOOK.
why: Only model-flagged elements can be replaced; the rest is covered by hooks and theming.

what: The kb guard warned that three consecutive searches ran without a kb lookup, while the builder was reading generated files and running CLI commands.
why: Guard triggers on source reads and shell calls, not on a kb-first plan.

what: Builder used ask_user to ask permission for the application-customizer.tsx exception. The orchestrator corrected it: never use ask_user, write everything to the common channel.
why: Orchestrator rule for this run: questions go to the common channel, not ask_user.
workaround: Continued without further asking; decision recorded in GAPS.md.

what: The generated table component builds the column customizer lookup filter with a missing closing parenthesis after (column=price), so the OSGi filter is invalid.
why: Generator bug in the table component template for customizer lookups; found when customImplementation was enabled on the table column.
workaround: Not patched (generated file). Table column left generated; logged in GAPS R1-1.

what: Browser tool: wait --text 'Hello' timed out even though the text was on the page, and wait @ref and wait --url also timed out on a loaded page.
why: Tool wait conditions do not match the rendered page reliably.
workaround: Took a fresh snapshot and clicked elements by ref instead of waiting.

what: Browser session repeatedly fell back to about:blank on its own. keyboard type wrote the quote characters literally, Tab did not move focus, and Meta+a and Control+a did not clear the field. Once the username lookup failed with 'Could not locate element'.
why: Browser tool issues: page state reset, literal key text, focus handling.
workaround: Reopened the URL, used the type command per field, logged the issue as a tool problem.

what: Builder used fixed waits (wait 4000, 5000, 6000 ms) while checking in the browser, against the round rule to wait for an element or URL.
why: Builder did not follow the round's check rule.

what: Built a shared price component in src/custom/components/Price.tsx (formatPrice gives two decimals plus EUR, e.g. 79.90 EUR). Registered it for the form and the view through application-customizer.tsx, which was added to .generator-ignore. The table column was skipped, logged in GAPS R1-1, and kept on customImplementation=false.
why: Table column hook could not be used (generator bug, see c02-04 and c02-09). Form and view could use the model flag plus CUSTOM_VISUAL_ELEMENT_INTERFACE_KEY.
workaround: Generated application-customizer.tsx edited (approved exception) and listed in .generator-ignore; table left on generated price format.

what: Builder's GAPS entry says the table-hooks.md column customizer example documents TABLE_COLUMN_CUSTOMIZER_HOOK_INTERFACE_KEY with {component, column} but does not say the hook works only when the DataColumn has customImplementation=true in the model.
why: Builder's reading of the doc; the doc lacks the model precondition.

what: Login attempts failed because the builder typed the password into the wrong field and used the wrong input commands (quoted text, keyboard inserttext mixed with type). The builder then had to retype the password.
why: Builder's own typing mix-up in the browser, not a server fault.
workaround: Cleared the fields and retyped both with the type command, then signed in.

what: Builder used eval to read document.activeElement while checking focus, which is outside the check rules. It said so in its notes.
why: Builder wanted to confirm focus state; the round rules ban eval for clicks and deep links, and this was a read.

what: The table-hooks.md column customizer example shows the hook as (original) => ..., but the shipped type is () => (original) => GridColDef, a factory that returns the transform. The builder logged the difference.
why: The catalog example signature does not match the shipped ColumnCustomizerHook type.
workaround: Followed the shipped type in the notes; the hook itself could not be used (see c02-04).

what: Builder states the catalog has no hook for a view or field display; ui-hooks.md covers only AppBar, hero, logo, footer and menu. The only route it found is a model-level custom implementation on the field.
why: ui-hooks.md scope does not list field or detail display hooks, so a price display on a plain DataField has no documented hook.
workaround: Used the model customImplementation flag on the form and view price fields.

what: Round 1 screenshots at 375, 768 and 1440 px all failed because checks/S04 did not exist. The builder then deleted the screenshots and wrote a README saying the round's checks were not completed.
why: Builder did not create the output folders before taking screenshots.
workaround: Created checks/S04 and checks/S09, then removed the partial screenshots and recorded the incomplete check in README.md.

what: Orchestrator confirmed the browser tool delivers no click events to the page (a capture listener saw zero clicks for ref, text and raw mouse). set viewport lags and open sometimes leaves the tab on about:blank. The browser tool was dropped for checks and the round moved to Playwright E2E. Also covers the round 1 menu entry that would not open after login, which the builder first took for an app bug.
why: Tool-level fault in agent-browser, not the app or the catalog. Explains the round 1 menu click failure.
workaround: Round 2: checks rewritten as Playwright E2E tests; browser tool no longer used for checks.

what: Builder first concluded the generated project had no application/e2e module. The catalog switch exists: README 'Prerequisites > Enable E2E Generation' says set generateE2eModule=true. The first kb search did not surface that section.
why: E2E generation is off by default (generateE2eModule=false in generator-parameter.properties); the kb section was not the top hit for the first query.
workaround: Set generateE2eModule=true in generator-parameter.properties, ran build; application/e2e/webshop__shop was generated.

what: Orchestrator directed that every browser check be a Playwright E2E test (login, menu, list, details, edit, back), with screenshots at 375, 768 and 1440 px. Table currency stays a logged gap unless a documented non-generated route appears.
why: Browser tool click delivery failed; E2E is the JUDO check method in agent-docs/e2e-testing.

what: Builder's macOS shell mistakes: the GNU timeout wrapper is not installed (timeout: command not found), a sed call on generator-parameter.properties used the wrong -i form, and it appended then removed a property line; the property ended up true.
why: Builder's own shell editing mistake; the property is a one-line change.
workaround: Re-ran sed with the correct form; grep confirmed generateE2eModule=true.

what: For the table price column, the builder chose a derived String attribute priceLabel on ProductInfo, getter self.price!round(2)!asString() + ' EUR', added as a DataColumn with fill --pages table, and removed the plain price column from the table. This puts the currency into the list without patching a generated file.
why: Column hook could not be used (c02-04). Kb search for a non-generated route led to derived attributes (literal-derived-attribute.md and the JQL function list in model-development.md).
workaround: Model change saved, generate and build run; see later items for build results.

what: judo fill --pages table added unrequested DataColumns (description and priceLabel) and changed dataFeature on them. The builder had to delete the description column by hand.
why: fill creates a column for every transfer object member, so the dry-run output had to be read before the real run.
workaround: Ran fill --dry-run first, then fill, then judo delete on the unwanted columns; the price column was removed on purpose.

what: Playwright chromium install hung for 10 minutes, then the downloaded Chromium binary was killed on launch (exit 137); every test failed with browserType.launch 'Unknown system error -88'.
why: Environment problem on this arm64 Mac with the playwright-managed Chromium build. Root cause not isolated.
workaround: Removed the cache and reinstalled; still failed. Wrote a local config (playwright.local.config.ts, not generated) that uses the installed Google Chrome channel.

what: Edit-form fill on the price input failed with 'element is not editable'. The cause was the builder's own PriceField, which set readOnly = !editMode while the view page starts with editMode false. The builder removed that condition and rebuilt.
why: Builder's component logic: read-only was tied to the page edit flag, which is false until the first change.
workaround: PriceField readOnly now only depends on __updateable; rebuilt and reran.

what: E2E selectors did not match the generated UI: getByLabel('Price') matched both the column menu button and the input, getByLabel('Name') matched more than one element, and 'Save' was used for the view update button, which is labelled 'Update'.
why: Builder guessed names; the catalog examples use icon-prefixed names and label-only lookups that are ambiguous on the list and form pages.
workaround: Changed the selectors to Update and to getByRole('textbox', { name }) with the helper names.

what: Round 2 report says there were several test runs and fixes in the end phase, although the round rule was to run the tests once at the end.
why: Builder ran the suite repeatedly to find selector and editability failures.

what: Orchestrator found the product descriptions are placeholder text 'a / b'. Real descriptions of 2 to 3 lines are required for the 3 products, entered through the UI in a test, not through SQL.
why: Builder seeded minimal test data for the description field.
workaround: Round 3 task: restore real descriptions through the UI.

what: Titles and menus still show internal names: 'ProductInfo Table', 'ProductInfo View / Edit', and the phone bottom bar shows 'ProductInfo' and 'Other'. Orchestrator requires user-facing labels 'Products' and 'Product'.
why: Model labels still carry the entity name; the builder had not set labels or i18n for the pages, menu and bottom bar.
workaround: Round 3 task: fix labels via model label and/or i18n, as the kb documents.

what: Builder removed .git/index.lock by hand after a git add failed, after checking pgrep. A lock file can belong to a running git process.
why: Builder's shortcut to finish the commit; the lock message said to make sure no git process ran.
workaround: Commit succeeded as b69df6a.

what: Session stopped just before the Round 2 report; the orchestrator resumed it and asked for the report again.
why: Session interruption, not a platform fault.
workaround: Resumed and wrote the report.

what: Model CLI element names and paths were guessed repeatedly: query ui MenuItem, Access, PageDefinition title, GraphQL menuItems and _type fields, and FQNs with the id: prefix all failed with 'does not exist' or 'element not found' before the right names were found.
why: The CLI and GraphQL type and field names differ between query, create and graphql, and the catalog does not list the working names for the navigation and page elements.
workaround: Read the GraphQL schema with graphql queries, then used FQNs from the query output (e.g. webshop::Shop::Menu for the menu label, ProductInfo_Table label via webshop::ProductInfo::ProductInfo_Table).

what: Phone bottom bar 'Other' label comes from the i18n key menuTree.other with default 'Other' in the generated BottomMenu. The kb has no section on it, so the builder read the generated source to find it.
why: Bottom-bar overflow label is a hard-coded i18n default that the catalog does not document.
workaround: Round 3: add an i18n override for menuTree.other via a generator override fragment (see c02-43).

what: Path and format of an i18n extra fragment for application_default.json were not in the kb. The builder first wrote the fragment under ui-react/actor/public/i18n with an unbraced JSON line, then found from the template jar that the path is actor/public/i18n/application_default_extra.fragment.hbs.
why: Best-practice page i18n-generator-override-extra-fragment.md says the path is project practice and not covered by agent-docs; the kb search did not return the template path.

what: judo move --dry-run printed the reordered element as 'changed ... description (in components)' rather than the element being moved, so the dry-run output was misread while reordering the form fields. The builder then ran discard --force to clear unsaved reorders.

workaround: Used move --json and graphql to confirm the child order, then discard --force and re-applied the move.

what: Field reorder did not reach the generated form and view. After move, relocate and row changes, the saved model showed Name, Price, Description, but the generated TSX and the generated UI model still listed price first, then name, then description. Orchestrator first reported the symptom in Round 2 (Price above Name on the details page).
why: Root cause given by the orchestrator in Round 4: the esm2ui ETL emits widgets per type in rule order, so number widgets come before text widgets; model order and row are ignored (see c02-55).
workaround: Pending; the builder tried delete and re-fill and update --add feature, see c02-49.

what: The kb has no section that says where the generated order of form and view fields comes from. The builder had to read the esm2ui transformation jar to learn it.

workaround: Read the tatami esm2ui ETL (esmToUi.etl) from the local jar.

what: The shipped esm2ui transformation is a compiled Java 'zeta' package without readable rules, so the builder could not see the exact rule that orders generated fields. Only the older ETL source was readable.

workaround: Logged in GAPS R3-1 as open; field order tests kept red.

what: Seeding the description through the UI with Playwright fill() did not store the value; the save response timed out. Switching to pressSequentially with a delay and a blur made the test pass.

what: Root cause of the field order bug (orchestrator, Round 5): esmToUi.etl sorts container children by ESM position (pre block ~line 77, post block ~line 114), but operations/ui/visualElement.eol:5 looks the position up with __pos.get(component) ?: 0. For these fields the lookup misses, so every position is 0 and the stable sort keeps rule-firing order, so number widgets come first. Groups inherit the order from their first child's rule.
why: Platform bug in the esm2ui transformation (judo-tatami-esm2ui, ETL position lookup). Earlier the orchestrator also cited dataField.etl rule order (Round 4) as the mechanism.
workaround: No workaround yet: Group wrappers tried in Round 4 did not change the order. Round 5: wrappers removed; the two field-order tests marked test.fail() with a comment naming the bug.

what: Orchestrator decided the two field-order tests stay in the suite but are marked test.fail() with a comment naming the platform bug, so the suite is green with a known failure. Wrapper groups from Round 4 are removed again.
why: Field order cannot be fixed by the model until the platform bug is fixed; the tests should document the gap, not block the suite.

what: Footwear products test expected Wool socks to be absent, but the earlier data left it in the list; the test depended on state from other runs.

what: Category Products shown as an inline to-many table on CategoryInfo View_Edit (representationComponent=table, with name, sku, priceLabel, unit columns) instead of the Products button, as the Round 7 correction asks.

what: Product image modelled as a BinaryType ProductImage (mime types image/png and image/jpeg, max 2 MB) on a STORED Product.image member.

what: Renaming the username member to email with a new type left the mapped member on the actor info transfer object with the old type; validate warned the data type must match its binding.

what: The Round 7 model script applied many CLI edits in one run with no check between steps; a partial run left unsaved edits, so the builder discarded them and reran the script.
why: CLI edits are applied one at a time, and a failing step does not roll back the earlier ones.

what: Stock status is a DERIVED string with a ternary getter (stock <= 0 gives Out of stock, below 5 gives Low, else In stock); category name is a DERIVED flattening self.category.name.

what: Admin actor added as a second actor with its own principal AdminAccountInfo (managed=false), branding copied from the shop, an EMAIL claim, products and categories accesses, and two menu entries.

what: Customer account created on first login by a custom AuthenticationInterceptor (CustomerProvisioningInterceptor) in the interceptors module; admin accounts are seeded on purpose, not created on login.

what: Generated actor modules (webshop__admin, webshop__customer) each get their own e2e module; the Level 0 Playwright tests had to be split across them by hand (git mv).

what: Playwright could not install chromium on this machine (it hangs on extraction), so the local config uses the installed Chrome channel and no retries.

workaround: playwright.local.config.ts sets channel chrome, workers 1, retries 0.

what: Seed script creates Keycloak users admin, customer1 and customer2, switches realm self sign-up on through the admin API, and seeds one AdminAccount row; customer rows are left to the first-login interceptor.

what: Seed upload through the generated binary input: setInputFiles set the file name in the textbox, but the test looked for an img inside the dialog and timed out.

what: Admin details page shows Price before Name and Description; the field order test failed, so the builder marked it test.fail() with a reason.
why: Generated view orders the number widget before the text widgets; same platform bug as the create form.
workaround: test.fail() with reason; the customer front has its own details layout that fixes the order.

what: Category products test found Running shoe twice (in the category view table and the product list), so the locator was ambiguous.
why: Same product shown in two grids on the page; locator was not scoped to the table.
workaround: Scoped the locator to the row and used exact name matching.

what: Admin product view cannot show the stored image: the generated binary field is an upload control that shows the file name, so the image test on the admin view was changed to check the file name.
why: The generated admin binary widget is an upload field; a picture view needs a custom display, which the customer front provides.
workaround: Admin test asserts the file name; the customer front shows the image through the generated ImageDisplay path.

what: Variant create dialog had no SKU textbox when the builder tried to fill it; the test timed out.
why: Dialog or button naming differed from the test expectation; the create button label is Ok in the inline dialog.
workaround: Changed the locator to the Ok button and reran.

what: Product images: the seed uploads a generated PNG per product through the file chooser; the customer card grid and details page show the real image (placeholder only without one); the admin view shows the file name.
why: Binary upload through the generated create dialog is the documented route; display in the customer front needs the token download.

what: Seed and card tests counted 9 products instead of 8 because a Temp product left by a failed F10 run stayed in the list.
why: Tests are not isolated; leftovers of failed runs are not removed before the seed count check.
workaround: Added a cleanup of Temp products to the admin seed, like an admin would.

what: Variant test: Delete matched two buttons (page header and variants table), and the header showed Update and Cancel instead of Delete while the product had unsaved changes.
why: Generated page shows Update and Cancel in edit mode; two Delete buttons exist when a table is on the view.
workaround: Cancel first when visible, then Delete with .first(); Escape in finally to close a stray dialog.

what: Variants and addresses inside a product or profile view are saved only with the page Update button; the tests failed until they clicked Update.
why: Composed child rows belong to the parent view and are stored with the parent save; the catalog does not say so next to the inline table pattern.
workaround: Tests click Update (saveView, saveProfile) after adding the child rows.

what: Variants table hidden on the customer product view by registering a custom implementation for the variants component; the admin keeps the inline table.
why: Customers should not see variant management; the customer details layout is custom code.

what: Customer addresses list via CustomerAccount!filter(...)!any().addresses showed only 2 of 6 stored addresses.
why: Cause not found in one kb-guided try; the !any() form on the composed list returned a partial list.
workaround: Replaced with Address!filter(a | a!container(CustomerAccount).email == ...) from the container back-reference pattern; the list then showed all addresses.

what: Customer profile is a singleton CustomerAccount found by its email from the login token; addresses are a composition of CustomerAccount, listed by a container back-reference getter, so one customer sees only their own rows.
why: Ownership must be enforced in the model; the back-reference pattern avoids a stored foreign key.

what: Interceptor provisioned a CustomerAccount row for admin@example.com because the admin user also logs in through the customer client; the decision was made on the client argument and the token azp had to be used instead.
why: The client argument passed to AuthenticationInterceptor is not the client id the builder expected; the catalog does not say what it contains.
workaround: Read the azp claim, logged the origin, and returned early for non-customer clients; a stray admin row was then removed.

what: A customer who opens the back office URL gets a User not found page instead of an access message.
why: The expected error for a wrong actor is not described in the catalog as far as the builder reported.
workaround: Reported as a known behaviour in the round report; no test change.

what: Customer products access filtered with Product!filter(p | p.active) so inactive products are missing from the shop; the admin access stays unfiltered.
why: Visibility must be enforced in the access getter, not in the frontend.

what: F16 test creates two new Keycloak sign-ups on each run; the data grows and the lists are paged, so the expectations depend on earlier runs.
why: Each run adds customers and addresses; the test does not clean up or isolate them.
workaround: Used unique names per run and exact cell matches; logged as GAPS R7-9c.

what: Whole Playwright suite was not run as one command: the admin and customer modules ran separately, and the last customer test edit was not followed by an admin re-run.
why: After the module split the suite has two roots; the builder ran each one, not the whole.
workaround: Reported the split runs in the round report.

what: Keycloak first-login row insert is not done by the runtime for the managed customer actor, so custom Java was needed.
why: Documented runtime limit: managed actor auto-insert is not implemented in the current runtime.
workaround: CustomerProvisioningInterceptor in application/interceptors.

what: Category filter test on the product table was marked test.fail() in Round 6 because a relation cannot be a top-level table column or filter without a derived attribute.
why: Catalog says a RelationColumn on a top-level table is a codegen bug; a flattened derived attribute is the documented route.
workaround: Marked test.fail() with reason; the Round 7 F12 derived categoryName removed the fail and added the filter.

what: Product image: ProductImage BinaryType (PNG, JPEG, 2 MB) on Product.image; seed uploads a PNG per product; customer grid and details show it; admin shows the file name; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch.

what: Variant composed in Product (label, SKU, stock), inline table on the admin product view, stored with Update; customer front hides the variants table; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch.

what: stockStatus DERIVED string (Out of stock, Low, In stock) from stock; shown in admin table and both details pages; nothing stored; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch.

what: ProductInfo.categoryName DERIVED from self.category.name; labelled Category; column and filter in the admin table; test.fail() removed; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch and F07 follow-up.

what: Customer sign-up through Keycloak registration page, CustomerProvisioningInterceptor creates the CustomerAccount on first customer login, seed script for keycloak users and realm sign-up; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch.

what: Two actors: Admin (back office, /webshop/Admin) and Customer (shop front, /webshop/Customer) with their own principals, claims, accesses, menus and generated modules; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch.

what: Customer products access filtered to active products (Product!filter(p | p.active)); admin access unfiltered; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch.

what: Customer profile singleton by email from token; own addresses via container back-reference getter; customer 1 and 2 never see each other's addresses; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch.

what: Footwear category page lists its products in an inline table (representationComponent table on CategoryInfo View_Edit), no Products button; commit 30914f0.
why: Round 7 follow-up.

what: The customer drawer looked squashed in the F09 1440 screenshot: labels cut to 'Pr...' and 'My...' and a tiny logo.
why: The screenshot helper resized the window and captured while the generated drawer was still animating its width, so the picture showed a mid-animation frame.
workaround: Helper waits until the logo reaches full width (settleLayout) before capturing at 1440; new drawer test checks labels and logo width.

what: The generated layout stores the mini drawer state in browser storage (webshop-config) and recomputes it only when the window crosses a size tier, so a browser that was once small opens collapsed on a desktop screen, also after reload.
why: Behaviour not described in the catalog; the builder searched the kb twice and found nothing on drawer state.
workaround: Render-nothing DrawerExpander registered as the documented AppBar extra component opens the drawer at lg and xl widths on load and on size change, in both actors.
proposed_target: generated layout drawer (miniDrawer persistence); document the workaround in ui-hooks.md

what: The customer API returned stock, active and variants on the product list and details (data leak), because the customer used the admin-facing product transfer object.
why: Own design mistake from earlier rounds: the customer product access pointed at the mapped ProductInfo, which carries admin-only fields.
workaround: New mapped transfer object ShopProductInfo without stock, active and variants; Customer.products points at it; ProductInfo stays admin only; test watches server answers for a browsing customer.

what: Renaming the customer product transfer object forced hand edits of custom frontend files (renamed custom-implementation file, new constants, container and type paths) and deletion of stale generated customer folders.
why: Custom frontend file names and constants are derived from the transfer object name; stale generated containers stay behind after a model change. The builder found the recovery steps in build-process.md.
workaround: git mv of the custom file, search-and-replace of names and paths, removal of generated pages, dialogs, containers and services folders, then regenerate.
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/deployment/build-process.md (renaming a transfer object: which generated and custom files follow)

what: Admin product table columns needed fixed widths at 1440 px, but the builder did not know the unit or value format of DataColumn.width and set plain integers (170, 120, 100 and so on).
why: The CLI schema shows width as a plain string; the catalog says fixed pixel width but the builder did not find a value example for the attribute.
workaround: Plain integer widths set on every column; all columns and row actions fit at 1440 and the admin tests now run at 1440.

what: The numeric price column cannot be shown formatted or sorted another documented way, so the admin table shows 79.9 and the builder only renamed the header to 'Price (EUR)' to fit it.
why: The DataColumn schema has formatValue and sort settings, but the builder found no documented way to format a numeric column value (R1-1 and R6-4 remain open).
workaround: Kept the numeric column with a shorter label and a width; formatting left open.

what: The CLI query for DataColumn and DataFilter returned nothing until 'fill' had been run on the transfer object, so the builder first thought the table columns did not exist.
why: Column and filter elements are created by fill, not by create; the query output gives no hint of that.
workaround: Ran fill on the transfer object, then queried again.
proposed_target: judo-cli query output or judo-cli.md note on fill

what: Creating a transfer object with a mapping auto-creates the mapped members (lineTotal, total and so on), so hand-made derived members with the same names gave 'not unique' and binding errors on validation.
why: Behaviour of mapped transfer objects not described where the builder looked; the same lesson was learned in R7 (R7-14) and repeated.
workaround: Deleted the duplicated hand-made members and kept the auto-created ones; validation passed.
proposed_target: catalog/best-practices/model/unmapped-transfer-dto.md or a mapped-transfer-object page: mapping creates members

what: Validator warnings appeared after the Customer product access changed: 'Columns are not defined for the viewable table' and 'Principal of actor Customer should not have relations and operations'.
why: Not explained by the builder; the warnings were noted in the CLI output and not acted on.

what: Running pnpm format by hand failed because the lockfile entries were newer than the minimumReleaseAge policy.
why: pnpm policy in the generated frontend rejects lockfile entries published within the cutoff; the real build failure was the duplicate import (c04-13), so this was a side issue in the investigation.
proposed_target: generated frontend pnpm configuration (minimumReleaseAge vs lockfile)

what: An OperationForm placed directly in a view fails UI validation (ActionContainerSameWithActionDefinition, NamedElementHaveToBeInApplication); the operation must sit in an ActionGroup, and the catalog says direct placement works.
why: The catalog section on operation wiring says OperationForm inside View or Form works; the transformation rejects it. The openspec sweep already lists ActionGroup-wrapped OperationForms as an open item (FR-033). Even inside an ActionGroup, the validator still reported action container errors after the wrap (session:L2494).
workaround: Moved both operations into an ActionGroup named actions, set label Actions and featuredActions=1; for checkout the action container errors cleared only after it became void with generateActionsHook=true (validation passed, session:L2522).
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/model/ui-authoring-guide.md section 10 (OperationForm in ActionGroup is required; constraints on action container)

what: postCallAccessNavigation cannot be cleared once set, and move --index had no effect on the position of the action group; move --after did reorder the menu entries.
why: CLI behaviour: unset is refused for this attribute and move with an index is ignored for these elements.
workaround: Left postCallAccessNavigation set (the clear attempt was refused, session:L2481); used move --after for menu order, since move --index had no effect.
proposed_target: judo-cli update and move (unset of postCallAccessNavigation, move --index)

what: An operation with an output and an input dialog makes the generated dialog file import the output type twice (import type { OrderInfo, OrderInfo, ... }); Biome rejects it as a parse error and the frontend build stops.
why: Generator bug. Tried mapped output, output with a relation to the same type, and output with one primitive: all failed the same way. The catalog's operation-return-type-navigation pattern (return the destination type from the operation output) is therefore blocked.
workaround: Made checkout a void operation; the new order is opened through the generated dialog actions hook (see c04-14).
proposed_target: generator: dialog types for operations whose output is also a post-call navigation target

what: Checkout is a void operation. The new order opens through the generated dialog actions hook (postCheckoutForCartInfoAction, generateActionsHook=true), which lists the newest order and navigates to it.
why: Only route left after the duplicate-import generator bug (c04-13); it costs one extra list call and deviates from FUNCTIONS F21 (operation returns the created order).
workaround: Java checkout is void; the hook navigates to the newest order.

what: A business fault shows in the generated fault dialog as the error code letter by letter (0: N, 1: O, 2: T ...), not as a readable message.
why: The generated 422 handler opens the dialog from the first key of the response body; the body starts with 'code', not the fault. The catalog describes the body with the fault key first, which is wrong for this version.
workaround: Error handler interceptor shows the fault's message as a snackbar (documented route in the frontend error-handling page).
proposed_target: generated error-handling.ts (422 handler takes first key); catalog body order in error-handling.md

what: Stock overflow is a modeled fault (ShopFault with message) declared on addToCart; the UI reads the message through a custom error interceptor and shows it as a snackbar.
why: Modeled faults are the documented business-error route (error-handling-guide); the generated dialog cannot show the message (c04-15).

what: After generate or build, target/judo-cli.jar disappeared, so every CLI call failed with 'Unable to access jarfile' until generate-root was run again.
why: generate and build do not recreate the CLI jar; only generate-root (or the validate goal) copies it. Known from earlier rounds (R7-7, S01).
workaround: Helper script .scratch/ensure-cli.sh runs generate-root when the jar is missing; used before every CLI step.
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/model/judo-cli.md (generate and build do not restore the jar)

what: The builder did not consult the kb before source searches: about 20 kb guard warnings ('repeated source searching, still no kb consult'); the orchestrator later counted kb 6 of 161 calls.
why: Builder habit: catalog and generated code were read with ctx_execute and grep instead of kb_search and kb_get first.

what: The builder said the kb had no entry for the generated DAO method names, error handler and customization constants; the DAO names were read from the generated SDK instead.
why: Claim is unverified: data-access-guide.md exists in the catalog and the builder read it at session:L2364 for another question. The kb-first search was not run for these names.
workaround: Read generated SDK and frontend source directly.

what: A reload added to the screenshot helper (to lay out the drawer) closed open dialogs, so six admin tests failed until the reload was removed.
why: Own test-helper mistake made while fixing R8-1.
workaround: Removed the reload calls from the helpers; admin suite then passed 30 of 30.

what: Card locators matched other products whose descriptions mention the product name ('Hiking socks' matched two cards), giving strict-mode violations in the F20 tests.
why: Locator by text, not by the exact card name.
workaround: card() helper filters by the exact card-name element.

what: The F19 and F20 tests waited for dialog buttons with names Add to cart, Ok, Check out, and then Submit; the wrong button names and the dialog expectation cost several test runs.
why: Test expectations written before the generated dialog labels were known.
workaround: Button regex changed to Ok or Submit; the readable error is checked as a snackbar text.

what: The admin and shop product counts read 9 instead of 8 in the S04 and S08 tests after the F01 category test failed, probably leaving an extra product behind.
why: Inferred from the sequence of failed runs (level1 F01 failed at session:L2577); not confirmed by the builder.

what: Menu order is not taken from the model: the drawer shows Products, My orders, My addresses, Cart, My profile although the model lists Cart second; move commands had no effect on the generated order.
why: Menu order is decided by the generated drawer; the builder did not use the menu customizer hook.

what: No catalog text found by the builder on whether a custom operation rolls back on error; the builder proved it with a test instead (stock of the first line restored when the second line throws a ShopFault).
why: The backend docs cover rollback for interceptors and for integration test modes (AUTO_ROLLBACK) but not the runtime rule for custom operations; the builder's kb search for the rule found nothing.
workaround: Integration-style Playwright test proves the rollback of stock, cart and order.

what: Order numbers come from the platform SEQUENCE variable (WS-year-six digits), not from the gap-free document-registry-sequence blueprint; a refused checkout does not use a number, but a number can gap after a rollback or crash.
why: The blueprint needs a lock and a registry entity; the platform sequence is simpler and the builder accepted gaps as documented in platform-behavior-reference.

what: The cart page is a custom component (Cart.tsx) that replaces the generated lines table and shows unit price, line total and total with the shared Price component; values come from the model's derived members (CartLine.lineTotal, CartInfo.total).
why: The generated lines table shows raw numbers (R1-1), and the Price component is the frontend quality bar from FUNCTIONS.md.

what: Add to cart on product cards and details page, via bound custom operation addToCart (Java, customer found by ACTOR email, DAO access); button disabled when out of stock.
why: Level 3 spec: cart belongs to the Customer; add goes on card or details.

what: Adding the same product again increases the quantity of the existing cart line; the operation re-fetches the entity.
why: Level 3 spec: one line with quantity 2.

what: Cart line total (quantity times price), cart total and line count derived in the model; empty cart shows 0.00 EUR; cart page in the Customer menu uses the shared Price component.
why: Level 3 spec: derived numeric with aggregation over a collection.

what: Quantity above stock throws the modeled ShopFault from addToCart; the UI shows a readable snackbar with the stock count and what is already in the cart; nothing is added.
why: Level 3 spec: business fault to readable UI error.

what: Checkout asks for a shipping address (CheckoutInput transfer object), creates the order from the cart, empties the cart and opens the new order via the dialog actions hook; the operation itself is void.
why: Level 3 spec: operation with input transfer object; the output form was blocked by the generator bug.
workaround: See c04-13 and c04-14.

what: Order lines copy product name and unit price at order time (snapshot fields on SalesOrderLine and OrderLineInfo); later price changes do not affect the order line.
why: Level 3 spec: snapshot attributes written by the operation.

what: Checkout decrements stock per line inside the one operation transaction; a test proves the rollback (stock restored, cart kept, no order) when a later line fails with a ShopFault.
why: Level 3 spec: prove the rollback with a test.

what: Order numbers WS-year-six digits from the SalesOrder platform sequence (VariableResolver SEQUENCE); test checks consecutive numbers. Admin gets a read-only Orders list (no create, update or delete).
why: Level 3 spec: order numbers and admin read only orders.

what: The customer drawer profile showed the generated login name instead of the customer's name.
why: The default hero props use preferredUsername, which is a generated string for sign-ups and tests.
workaround: CustomHeroPropsHook in registerShellHooks.ts: given and family name from the token, then e-mail, then login name.

what: The documented menu reorder example sorts by item ids such as dashboard, but generated menu ids are long model ids, so the example cannot be used as written.
why: The catalog example does not show the real id format of generated menu items.
workaround: Sorted the menu by item title (Products, Cart, My orders, My profile, My addresses) in registerShellHooks.ts; test checks the five labels.

what: Builder read or grepped generated code (SDK, frontend services, customization files) many times after the kb had no answer or was skipped; the kb guard warned about several consecutive source searches roughly fifteen times in the round.
why: kb-first rule not applied consistently; the kb share was low (orchestrator: 19 of 168 calls).
workaround: Recovered by reading the kb after each warning; catalog answers were found for most later lookups.

what: A 0..1 relation query returns Optional<Product>, while a 1..1 relation query returns the entity; the first build failed with a type mismatch because the builder assumed Optional.
why: The kb says single-valued relation queries return the entity but does not separate optional (0..1) from mandatory (1..1) relations.
workaround: Used the entity directly for the 1..1 cart line product relation (RemoveProductCustomImplementation.java).

what: The per-relation createHistory method did not exist until the relation had createable=true, which the builder only found after a failed build.
why: relation-based-entity-creation.md states the createable rule in one sentence that the builder missed on first read.
workaround: Set createable=true on SalesOrder.history in the model, then the generated create method appeared.

what: FUNCTIONS.md specifies the order status history as a post-call interceptor, which cannot fire for custom transition operations.
why: Interceptors run only for built-in operations; the spec was written without checking that rule, while the catalog states it correctly.
workaround: Each transition writes its history row inside the custom operation (OrderLifecycle.transition), in the same transaction.

what: FUNCTIONS.md specifies a range interceptor for the default 30-day order filter, but range interceptors fire only on reference range operations, not on list calls.
why: The spec assumed an interceptor could restrict a plain list; the catalog says a list needs an access definition or a list interceptor.
workaround: Modelled Admin.orders as a DERIVED access (orderedAt later than now minus 30 days) and added Admin.allOrders (ALL) so older orders stay reachable.

what: No documented way to backdate or seed an old order in a running-app Playwright test, so the 30-day cut-off itself is untested.
why: Order timestamps are set only by checkout; the initializer has no documented trigger; the kb fixture examples are for Java integration tests, not the running app.
workaround: Test checks that today's order is in the 30-day list and in All orders; the cut-off is left untested and logged.
proposed_target: catalog/best-practices/backend/init-data-seeding.md (seed or backdate rows for running-app tests)

what: FUNCTIONS.md says delete deactivates a product that has orders; the catalog pattern refuses the delete with a fault and leaves deactivation to the user.
why: Spec and catalog pattern disagree on the behaviour.
workaround: Followed FUNCTIONS.md: removeProduct deactivates when orders exist; generic delete switched off (deleteable=false), removeProduct is the only delete.

what: After a successful removeProduct, the generated page says the operation succeeded, refreshes the deleted product (404 BOUND_OPERATION_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND) and never opens the output dialog.
why: Generated post-operation flow refreshes the bound instance after an operation that deletes it.
workaround: Page actions hook registerProductRemovedHook.ts (documented postRemoveProductForProductInfoAction): shows the returned message and goes back to the product list.
proposed_target: generated admin page flow for operations that delete the bound instance

what: F29 test created a product with SKU T-514769, which breaks the model pattern for SKU, so the create failed and the test failed.
why: Test built the SKU from the product name and clock digits without checking the SKU pattern in the model.
workaround: SKU now uses a TL or TT prefix with four digits from the stamp.

what: Every run of the F29 test leaves one inactive Temp tent product in the admin list, because the product with orders cannot be deleted.
why: No documented way to remove orders, so the test data cannot be cleaned up.
workaround: Logged as known; later round (R10) switched the test to a seeded product.

what: Admin F10 test clicked the page Delete button; after the generic delete was switched off the test timed out.
why: Generic delete removed by the F29 model change (deleteable=false) and the test selector was not updated.
workaround: Selector changed to the Delete product button and the Yes confirmation.

what: no-admin-data customer test failed: it read response bodies asynchronously and asserted before they were collected (expected 2, got 1).
why: Race in the test: response text is read after the assertion.
workaround: expect.poll on the body count; test passes when re-run.

what: Customer spec imported helpers from the admin Playwright package, which loaded a second copy of @playwright/test; Playwright then reported No tests found.
why: Shared helpers across actor packages are not documented as a supported pattern in the e2e docs.
workaround: Copied the needed helper functions into the customer spec.

what: Existing Postgres volume was not migrated after the model added SalesOrderLine.product: queries failed with column c_product_id does not exist. ./judo.sh schema-upgrade then failed (SCHEMA_DIR empty, Maven cannot read the schema project), so the containers and both volumes were wiped and re-seeded; this repeats the R6-1 gap for the third round.
why: Generated judo.sh schema-upgrade path bug; the catalog says a development database needs no step, which does not hold for an existing volume with data.
workaround: Wipe containers and volumes, restart, scripts/seed-dev-user.sh, seed tests (repeated in R10 with the same failure).

what: A plain ./judo.sh build after generate failed with There are manual changes in the generated files (frontend files reformatted), although git showed no change; the build passed with -i.
why: Frontend build reformats generated files and the generator then treats them as hand-edited; cause not found by the builder.
workaround: ./judo.sh build -i (the checksum-mismatch option from agent-docs/frontend/README.md).
proposed_target: frontend build checksum handling after generate

what: A model edit script was run a second time without discard, so every element was created twice; validate reported 38, then 50 errors. discard refused without --force.
why: Script was not idempotent and the builder did not check unsaved CLI state before re-running it.
workaround: discard --force, then one clean run of the script.

what: judo-cli query --select on a reference field (target, access, hiddenBy, enabledBy, postCallAccessNavigation) fails with SubselectionRequired; a query written to a file once came back as blank whitespace.
why: CLI requires a sub-selection for reference fields; the error does not say which fields to select.
workaround: Re-ran the query with explicit sub-selections or printed to stdout.

what: create -t Access also creates a MenuItemAccess named Menu_n labelled with the target type name (AdminOrderInfo), so duplicate menu entries and not-unique errors followed; deleting an access referenced by a menu needs --cascade.
why: Side effects of Access creation are not documented for the CLI.
workaround: Deleted the duplicate access and menu, re-created one access, relabelled the menu.

what: create -t ActionGroup without a parent was refused (Cannot create ActionGroup in Model); the group must be created with --ns of the view, then operations are relocated into it.
why: The ui-authoring-guide says an OperationForm inside a view works, but gives no CLI recipe for the ActionGroup.
workaround: create -t ActionGroup -n actions --ns <view>, then relocate each operation into it.

what: Repeated shell slips: head -0 errors, a log file never written because of a brace redirect (ENOENT twice), a script line that referenced an element created later, and a broad find over the home folder that timed out after 60 seconds.
why: Hand-written shell scripts and broad searches.
workaround: Re-ran with correct paths and order.

what: Tool output wrapper replaced larger outputs with search stubs, so the builder re-ran commands; ctx_execute also rejected an unknown timeout argument.
why: Context-mode wrapper behaviour and tool argument schema.
workaround: Re-ran commands with output written to files; dropped the bad argument.
proposed_target: context-mode output stubs and ctx_execute argument schema

what: Validator warned that the principal of actor Customer should not have relations and operations; the builder did not address the warning.
why: Principal rule for actors with relations is not explained in the catalog pages the builder read.
workaround: None; warning left in place.

what: History rows show the login e-mail as the actor, not a person's name.
why: ACTOR variable gives the e-mail; no documented way to show a name in a history row was found.
workaround: Left as is and logged as open.

what: History rows are written by OrderLifecycle.transition (actor = ACTOR e-mail, what = status change, when = now) in the same transaction; a refused transition writes nothing; checkout writes Order placed.
why: Custom operations never reach interceptors, and the audit blueprint says the operation itself must write the row.

what: Transition buttons are hidden with hiddenBy on derived booleans on the order (payHidden, shipHidden and so on); the tracking number is an input of the ship operation and is hidden on the order unless SHIPPED or DELIVERED; the server also refuses invalid moves.
why: Derived booleans give valid buttons without a frontend hook; the server check protects against stale UI.

what: Two order transfer objects: AdminOrderInfo (all transitions, tracking, history, customer e-mail) for the admin and OrderInfo (cancel on NEW only) for the customer.
why: Customer must never see admin buttons; same idea as the product split in R8.

what: Interceptors fire only for built-in create, update, delete and reference operations; custom, mapped and script operations never reach them, so their guards and audit rows must sit inside the operation.
why: Stated by the builder from the kb and checked against interceptors.md; the catalog already says it.

what: Range interceptors (getRangeFor and _getRangeReference) fire only on reference range lookups, not on plain list calls such as ~list.
why: Stated in interceptor-range-override.md; the builder relied on it to reject the FUNCTIONS.md design.

what: F25 order status NEW to PAID to SHIPPED to DELIVERED or CANCELLED: OrderStatus enum and one custom operation per transition on AdminOrderInfo (Pay, Ship, Deliver, Cancel).
why: Enumeration state machine pattern.

what: F26 only valid transitions are offered: derived hide booleans feed hiddenBy on each action; invalid moves refused with INVALID_TRANSITION fault.
why: Operation enabled and hidden derivation from the enum state machine pattern.

what: F27 customer cancels an own NEW order; ownership and state checked in Java; cancelling returns the stock. Admin can also cancel PAID orders.
why: Role-guarded write plus state guard inside the custom operation.

what: Round 9 fixes: drawer profile name (CustomHeroPropsHook), menu order by title (MenuItemsCustomizerHook), and DAO docs read before the Java.

what: Order history on the admin view was not sorted by time (Shipped to Delivered listed before Order placed).
why: The history column had no default sort; the builder did not set one in R9.
workaround: Set sort=ASC on the history column happenedAt (DataColumn sort); test checks the four rows in time order.

what: The Ordered field on the admin order view showed a date picker icon although it should be read-only; a derived boolean in enabledBy greyed it out but left the picker.
why: The kb has no read-only switch for a mapped timestamp field; isReadOnly exists only for derived members.
workaround: Derived string orderedAtLabel replaces the field on both order views (sorting keeps the real timestamp); test checks a text box with no date group or picker button.

what: No runnable recipe in the kb for a Markdown Handlebars template rendered to PDF; the only document pipeline in the kb is the DOCX XDocReport one.
why: Catalog covers Handlebars email rendering, file store transfer and inline preview, but no Markdown to PDF step.
workaround: invoice.md.hbs rendered with Handlebars 4.2.0 (already in runtime), turned into PDF by a small Markdown renderer on PDFBox 2.0.13 (already in runtime), stored via FileStoreService, returned as FileType.

what: The XDocReport DOCX pipeline blueprint is still presented as a current pattern with no deprecation note, although the project lead says the pipeline is deprecated.
why: Blueprint status fields say single-project and do not mark deprecation.
workaround: Not used; a Markdown route was built instead.

what: Platform-provided libraries (PDFBox, Handlebars, FileStoreService) do not compile in the app module until the app pom declares them; the first build failed with unresolved imports.
why: Catalog does not say that runtime-provided libraries still need a compile-time dependency in the app module.
workaround: Added pom.xml.extra-dependencies.fragment.hbs (documented fragment slot), then build -i succeeded.

what: The Karaf runtime already contains PDFBox 2.0.13 and Handlebars 4.2.0 (karaf-offline assembly and karaf features), so no new bundle is needed for an invoice renderer.
why: Found by searching the built runtime; the catalog has no list of runtime-provided libraries.

what: application_hu-HU.json is not generated: the generator emits only application_en-US.json for this one-language model, while the i18n doc says every application_<locale>.json, including hu-HU, is generated from the model.
why: Catalog statement is wrong for a model with one language.
workaround: scripts/make-hu-translations.py builds the Hungarian file from the generated English file (about 190 labels translated; the rest English).

what: The generated locale map in l10n-context.tsx allows only en-US, and no date-fns locale exists for Hungarian, so the language switch needs a cast and date pickers stay English.
why: i18n Adding New Languages steps copy JSON files and update the selector but do not mention the locales map.
workaround: Language switch uses the documented L10N setLocale with a cast; date formatting left English.

what: The header tracks only one AppBarExtraComponents service, while ui-hooks.md shows several AppBar components; the drawer fix and the language switch had to be merged into one component.
why: Generated HeaderContent uses a single useTrackService lookup.
workaround: AppBarExtras.tsx combines DrawerExpander and LanguageSwitch and is registered once.

what: Model-built label strings (for example the order total label and line labels) stay in English with EUR format in Hungarian, because model expressions cannot pick the UI language.
why: Derived string members are fixed text; the Price component is the only locale-aware formatter.
workaround: Left as is; logged. Customer cart and shop use the Price component.

what: After Apply coupon or Remove coupon the generated cart page does not give the custom cart summary component new data, so the total stayed stale.
why: Post-operation flow does not refresh custom visual components.
workaround: Post-operation hooks dispatch a window event; the cart component listens and reloads; cart component also reloads on new signed identifier.
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/frontend/hooks/action-hooks.md (refresh of custom components after an operation)

what: Admin build log shows XMI ID COLLISION DETECTED errors (ten lines) for the e2e and frontend model; the build still succeeds.
why: Cause not investigated by the builder.

what: Field order on the order views: new fields are appended, so Total sits before Ship to and Coupon last on the admin order view.

workaround: move used for Ordered only; not tidied.

what: The same timestamp is shown in two time zones: Ordered reads 02:03 while history rows of the same order read 03:03.
why: Model and browser time zone handling differ from the JVM zone used in custom Java.

what: Invoice and coupon actions were placed directly into the view again (OperationForm outside an ActionGroup), giving ActionContainerSameWithActionDefinition and NamedElementHaveToBeInApplication errors.

what: F29 test failed with ReferenceError: reactivate is not defined after a cleanup block was pasted into the wrong test.

what: After the wipe, the admin product list showed 9 products where the seed test expects 8, and paging expected 3 rows on page 2 but found 4: the stray Temp tent product from F29 test runs.

what: The shop settings singleton has no startup seed: the model blueprint says the row is seeded by an initializer, but no startup trigger is documented, so the admin enters it once through the UI and a second row is not prevented by the model.
why: Catalog gives no trigger for init operations and no rule for singleton duplicates in the running app.
