what: Browser tests cannot set the business clock: WEBSHOP_BUSINESS_DATE is read once at class load, so it needs an application restart.
why: Catalog documents a start-up override for the injectable clock; no way to set it per test was found.
workaround: Tests use real dates around today (expired is yesterday, not yet valid is in two days).

what: Sale price window uses Date!now() in the model, so it follows the platform clock, not the business clock used by custom Java.
why: Model expressions cannot call the Java clock; the catalog says so.
workaround: Window tests use dates around today; the cart and order read the derived effectivePrice, so display, cart and order agree.

what: Coupon codes are stored on the cart as code plus percent (no relation), revalidated at checkout (clock, usage, minimum), and a use is counted in the checkout transaction; five distinct refusal codes.
why: Checkout must not accept a coupon that expired or was used up after it was applied; no relation keeps the cart simple.

what: BusinessClock class reads WEBSHOP_BUSINESS_DATE (env or system property) once at class load; checkout, order date and history use it; model expressions keep the platform clock.
why: Catalog pattern for one clock in Java; browser tests cannot change it, so tests use real dates.

what: Least-bad invoice route: Handlebars Markdown template, own Markdown-to-PDF renderer on PDFBox, FileStoreService put, FileType output, inline PDF dialog; DOCX pipeline not used.
why: Project lead says DOCX/XDocReport is deprecated; kb has no runnable Markdown to PDF recipe.

what: Hungarian application file is built by scripts/make-hu-translations.py as a new file (not a generated file), so no .generator-ignore entry; the script keeps every generated key and falls back to English.
why: Generator emits only en-US for this model; a new file with a new name needs no ignore entry.

what: Product prices are gross (VAT included): VAT = gross x rate / (100 + rate), net = goods minus discount minus VAT; VAT rate per category with a default.
why: Shop prices shown to customers include VAT; net and VAT are derived from gross.

what: Shop settings are one ShopConfig row entered through the admin UI by a seed test (no startup initializer), with create and update but no delete.
why: No documented startup trigger for an initializer (see c05-60).

what: F31 history sorted oldest first and Ordered shown read-only as derived text (orderedAtLabel) on both order views.
why: DataColumn sort ASC and derived string replace the date picker.

what: F33 shop configuration singleton (ShopConfig): shop name, free-shipping threshold, shipping fee, low-stock threshold, default VAT; admin menu Shop settings.
why: Singleton entity edited from one menu item.

what: F34 VAT rate per category; cart and order show goods, discount, net, VAT, shipping and total; order keeps per-line VAT.
why: Derived arithmetic across relations with stored order amounts.

what: F35 flat shipping fee below the free-shipping threshold read from the singleton in a derived expression; free at or above it.
why: Derived value reading the singleton.

what: F36 coupons: admin Coupons menu; customer applies or removes a code in the cart; five distinct refusal messages; re-checked and counted at checkout.
why: Entity plus custom validation in the operation with an injectable clock.

what: F37 sale price with a date window on the product; cards show sale price, struck-through regular price and a Sale chip; cart and order use the sale price only inside the window.
why: Derived member using the current date.

what: F38 low-stock list for the admin: derived access filtered by stock below the settings threshold; changing the threshold changes the list.
why: Filtered derived access reading the singleton.

what: F39 invoice PDF on paid, shipped and delivered orders for customer and admin; PDF opens inline in a dialog; test checks the PDF content.
why: Handlebars Markdown template plus PDFBox renderer, FileStore, inline download.

what: F40 English and Hungarian switch in the header of both actors; shared Price component formats with Intl (79,90 EUR in Hungarian); menus, buttons and cart labels translated.
why: i18n language switch registered as one AppBar extra; Intl formatting follows i18n language.

what: A derived flag written as a JQL negation on a boolean (filter with !n.read) failed to parse; the builder then used n.read == false.
why: Builder used a negation form without checking the kb first; the catalog documents the 'not' keyword in model-development.md.
workaround: Rewrote the expression as n.read == false.

what: Transform failed on a derived attribute that filters over a two-way collection (Product.wishedBy): 'Feature wishedBy not found', then an ObjectFilterExpression cannot be cast to CollectionExpression error in asm2expression.
why: Not explained in the chunk; occurred when a derived flag filtered the reverse side of a many-to-many two-way relation.
workaround: Set wishedBy cardinality to 0..* and re-created the derived flag with a different expression; some derived flags were removed and rebuilt.

what: validate reported 46 'Named element X is not unique in its container' errors after the model edit script ran twice on top of partly applied changes; discard refused without --force and the validate output dumped the EVL path instead of the failing element.
why: Non-idempotent create script re-run after a failed run without discarding; CLI discard requires --force and the error text is not actionable.
workaround: discard --force, then re-ran the script from a clean model.

what: judo query rejected field names the builder guessed (cardinality on Access, claimType on ActorType, target without a subselection); the error lists the valid fields but guessing cost several calls.
why: CLI query has no field discovery beyond the error text; target needs a subselection.
workaround: Read the valid field list from the error and used the GraphQL-style subselection.

what: create -t MimeType with -n failed ('name' not defined for MimeTypeCreateInput), and the --brief 'valid' output printed Java object strings (MimeTypeImpl@hash) instead of names.
why: CLI create for MimeType takes no name; the list of valid values is not rendered.
workaround: Created the MimeType with --ns only and kept the default name.

what: judo.sh generate clean-deletes the target folder, which removes target/judo-cli.jar, so the model CLI fails with 'Unable to access jarfile' until generate-root is run again.
why: generate runs a maven clean that also removes the CLI jar in target/.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh generate-root to restore the jar before using the CLI.

what: After a table operation was added to ProductInfo_Table, the build failed with XMI ID collisions on admin tabular reference actions and a UI generator NullPointerException (ActionDefinition.getIsExportAction null) on CategoryInfo Products RelationTablePage. Removing the operation fixed the build.
why: Not explained in the chunk; the NPE was in a generated page of a different entity than the one changed.
workaround: Deleted the ProductInfo table operation (delete --cascade) and created the import operation on a new ImportedProductInfo transfer object with a Products table operation.

what: Table operation names are not the short names the builder used (exportOrders vs exportOrdersTableOperation::exportOrders), and ui query has no TableOperation type, so updates failed with 'element not found'.
why: Operation element naming of table actions is not obvious from the CLI output.
workaround: Listed the table operations with query esm TableOperation and used the full names.

what: validate --strict reported errors after a delete with --no-check, but the same command still ran save, so an invalid model was written to disk.
why: save does not stop when validation fails in the same command chain; the builder chained them.
workaround: Re-ran delete --cascade and validation until clean.

what: The generated file upload button in the admin import dialog has only a title ('Upload file') and wraps a hidden file input, so getByRole('button', name) cannot find it in Playwright; getByTitle works.
why: Generated BinaryInput widget gives the upload control no accessible name.
workaround: Test uses getByTitle('Upload file') and the file chooser event.

what: In the generated export dialog, keys typed into the date range fields in one burst were lost, and typing into the second date field reset the first in form state (the request sent only toDate or only fromDate).
why: Builder's diagnosis: generated date widget loses input when typed fast and the second field resets the first.
workaround: Test types the date in segments with a pause, waits for the template request, and waits 1.5 s before typing; the until filter was dropped from the test.

what: The CSV export custom operation threw a NullPointerException on input.getFromDate().orElse(...) when the user left the date empty, because the optional input getter returned null, not Optional.empty.
why: Custom operation input getters for optional attributes can return null; the agent-docs custom-operations page does not say this where the builder looked, and the sweep inventory (BA-042) already flagged it.
workaround: Null-guarded the getters and the status filter in ExportOrdersCustomImplementation.

what: Builder claimed a write made in a postCall interceptor on the notification refresh was not kept: the log said 'marked as read' but the database kept c_read = f.
why: Builder did not isolate the cause; catalog says postCall runs in the transaction and rolls back the write on exception, which does not explain a silent drop.
workaround: Moved the read marking to a custom operation markRead called from the page post-refresh hook (see c06-14).

what: Notification read state is set by a custom operation markRead on NotificationInfo, called from the documented post-refresh page hook; the interceptor was removed.
why: Interceptor write was not persisted (c06-13); custom operations are not intercepted, so the operation is explicit.

what: The 'Ordered' text and history times differed by two hours: the model-built string orderedAtLabel used the platform zone (UTC), while the generated history column rendered in the browser zone (CET).
why: Model expressions follow the platform defaultZoneId, the UI follows the browser; the catalog says so but gives no model-side way to show the browser zone. Container is UTC, host CET; default zone already UTC so storage needed no change.
workaround: Removed the derived string; see c06-16.

what: 'Ordered' is the real timestamp shown by a read-only custom LocalTimestamp component in the browser zone (customer and admin), formatted without 12-hour clock; the test checks it equals the 'Order placed' history row.
why: Browser zone display matches the generated history column; no model change needed.

what: 'Ordered' is a custom field and the generator draws custom fields after the generated ones, so after the move it sits just above the buttons; field order in the order view is not fully controllable.
why: Custom fields are placed after generated fields; the field-order platform bug may apply.
workaround: Used the CLI move command to reorder the generated fields; left Ordered last.

what: A derived effectivePrice Price value on WishlistItemInfo was replaced by a derived string priceLabel with ' EUR' appended; the reason for the change is not stated in the chunk.
why: Not stated in the chunk.
workaround: Replaced effectivePrice with priceLabel (String) on the wishlist table and view.

what: Customer view fields that the page must load but not show (effectivePrice, onSale, ratingLabel, image, sale fields) were hidden with customImplementation=true and render-nothing components, because no view-field hook exists.
why: ui-hooks.md covers AppBar, hero, logo, footer and menu only; the only mechanism is a model-level custom implementation (already logged as a gap).
workaround: Layout-only components render the values in ProductDetailsLayout and CatalogHome.

what: Playwright suite failures from test design: the S11 details test opened the first product card, whose order is not fixed, and the admin 'Products' button matched two elements after the menu change.
why: Tests relied on grid order and on an ambiguous accessible name.
workaround: Opened the 'Running shoe' card by name; used an exact or specific locator.

what: Admin test for the unit dropdown flaked: Escape sometimes closes the whole dialog, so the later Back click timed out.
why: Test pressed Escape to close the option list, which also closes the dialog sometimes.
workaround: Test tolerates a closed dialog; re-run passed.

what: CSV import test used SKUs like IMP-A-<timestamp>, which fail the Product SKU pattern ^[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{4}$; the import of the bad row caused a PATTERN_VALIDATION_FAILED error.
why: Test fixture did not follow the model pattern.
workaround: Changed fixture SKUs to IA-<tag>, IB-<tag>.

what: Database not migrated for the new tables and columns; ./judo.sh schema-upgrade fails with a Maven ProjectBuildingException, so the containers and volumes were wiped and all earlier data is gone.
why: Known platform issue (R6-1, R10-3); the schema-evolution route in the kb does not work on this project.
workaround: Wiped containers and volumes, restarted, reran seed-dev-user.sh.

what: CSV export and import are custom operations that exchange the file through the file store; a small Csv helper quotes fields on write and parses on read; import checks all rows before creating any.
why: Matches the catalog bulk-csv pattern (file store, rows validated first).

what: Invite admin is a custom operation that normalizes the e-mail (trim and lower case) and writes through the principal TO's DAO, so the managed realm sync applies; the TO keeps its own admin projection.
why: Managed-actor pattern: the sync is bound to the principal TO's DAO, not to the entity.

what: Own compile error: isBlank and trim called on Optional<String> returned by input.getName() in InviteAdminCustomImplementation.
why: Builder assumed a plain String getter; the generated getter returns Optional.
workaround: Used getName().map(trim).filter(not empty).orElse(email).

what: Builder found the FileStoreService API by unzipping and javap of jars, although the catalog covers the file store pattern.
why: Did not search the kb for the file store API first.
workaround: Read the interface with javap.

what: Kb discipline: 10 kb_search and 5 kb_get calls against 208 bash and 45 read calls; the kb guard warned 52 times that source searching ran without a kb check; generated code and jars were read before the kb was consulted.

what: ./judo.sh schema-upgrade fails with ProjectBuildingException because SCHEMA_DIR defaults to the model directory (project root), so the schema POM path is <root>/schema. Setting schema_dir=application makes it run, but no catalog page says schema_dir exists.
why: judo.sh derives SCHEMA_DIR from model_dir; in this layout the schema module lives under application/, and the catalog does not document schema_dir.
workaround: Ran schema_dir=application ./judo.sh schema-upgrade, and later the generate/execute route (see c07 F52 decision).

why: The command table describes schema-upgrade as generate-and-apply; the backfill route needs generate, edit, then execute as separate steps.
workaround: Used judo-rdbms-schema:generate with the old model file, wrote 06_updateDataAfterIncremental by hand, then :execute.

what: F52 migration without a wipe: copy the pre-change RDBMS model and pg_dump first, generate the migration with the old model as base, hand-write the weight and returnWindowDays backfill in changeset 06, then execute. Products, settings and orders survived.
why: schema-upgrade cannot host the backfill, and the user asked for a documented route with no wipe.

what: Migration with data: weight (backfilled 500) and ShopConfig.returnWindowDays (backfilled 14) in migration 1, then a second migration adding stored soldUnits with an SQL backfill. Fixture test compares pre-migration products with the table.
why: Built per the user's F52 request.

what: Bulk price change: a Change prices row action on each category (instance operation with a percent input), one transaction, 2-decimal rounding, rejects 0, -100 or less, +1000 or more, changes list price only, hand-written audit rows, success snackbar.
why: Built per the F45 row.

what: Bulk price change is an instance row action on the category table, not a static collection operation.
why: Static collection operations on shared tables hit a generator bug seen in R11 (R11-7c).

what: Admin dashboard: DashboardInfo over the settings row with orders today, revenue today (cancelled excluded, shared price format), and top 5 best sellers by stored soldUnits with rowsPerPage 5.
why: Built per the F48 row.

what: Sorting by a derived aggregate gives a generated-SQL error (missing FROM-clause entry), and a nested filter or filter plus sort over the same type gives 'table name _iterator_N specified more than once' at runtime (HTTP 500 on the dashboard and on coupon creation).
why: Platform JQL-to-SQL generator bug for these expression shapes.

what: The top-N expression form is unclear: !sort(...)!heads(5) fails in asm2query with 'Missing variable name', and !heads(p | ..., 5) validates but returns only one row at runtime. The catalog lists !heads(n) without a working top-N example.

what: soldUnits is a STORED aggregate kept by checkout, cancel and return approval, instead of a derived sum, so the dashboard can sort it.

what: Returns: ReturnRequest owned by the order line (REQUESTED to APPROVED or REJECTED), window from delivery plus ShopConfig.returnWindowDays (default 14), approval restores stock and writes a history row with the refund, pages Return an item, My returns and Returns to review.

what: The Request return button exists only inside the window because a row action cannot be hidden per row (CLI rejects hiddenBy), so returnable lines get their own page.

what: The CLI rejects hiddenBy and enabledBy on a TableOperation ('not defined for input object type TableOperationUpdateInput'), although tables-navigation.md lists both properties for ui:TableOperation.

what: The label of a row action must be set on the operation form element (TableOperation::<op>::<op>), not on the TableOperation. Setting label on the TableOperation or on a guessed element name failed with 'element not found' or 'label not defined'.

what: The wishlist price came from a derived string (priceLabel = price plus ' EUR' in the model), so it was not localised and the generated numeric column showed a number without currency. The shared Price component cannot be placed on a generated table column.

what: The table column customizer hook key is imported by the generated tables but nothing consumes it, so a hook registered for a column never applies. The catalog's Custom Columns section presents it as working.
why: Grep over the generated frontend found no consumer of TABLE_COLUMN_CUSTOMIZER_HOOK_INTERFACE_KEY; the platform does not wire it.

what: Setting DataColumn.customImplementation=true makes the generated table use useTrackService without importing it, so pnpm build fails with TS2304 in every such table. The builder also reports that TransferObjectTable.customImplementation is accepted by the CLI and does nothing.
why: Generator emits a call to a hook it does not import; the table-level flag has no effect in the generated code.
workaround: Reverted customImplementation on the columns, set it only on the table, then used a custom view page.
proposed_target: generator: DataColumn customImplementation emits useTrackService without import; TransferObjectTable.customImplementation no-op

what: Wishlist is a view page of a new TransferObjectType WishlistInfo (access Customer.myWishlist, 0..1) whose items element is a custom implementation, following the cart pattern. The generated wishlist access is kept for move and remove.
why: Column hooks and column customImplementation do not work (see the two platform-bug items).

what: Wishlist page uses the shared Price component ('12,00 EUR' in Hungarian), with loading, empty and error states, Move to cart and Remove through the generated service.

what: Notifications header: the bell navigates with clearNavigate so the breadcrumb reads Home, and AppBarExtras wraps the language switch and the bell in one flex row with no stray background.

what: In the drawer, the generated layout stacks the AppBar extra components as a column, so the bell button stretched over the full drawer width and showed as a grey ellipse.
why: Generated layout of AppBar extra components has no documented row layout; the builder fixed it by wrapping them in one Box.
workaround: One flex Box wrapper inside AppBarExtras.

what: Shop branding (logo, title, primary colour) stays in the model. It is not read from the configuration singleton. A test checks logo and colour on five pages per app.
why: Theme colours are ActorType attributes and the logo and title are model elements, all applied at build time; editing palette.ts would need a .generator-ignore entry, which is forbidden.
workaround: Documented the decision and checked it in tests.

what: Builder claims there is no documented way to read brand values from a runtime settings row; palette and logo are fixed at start-up.
why: Builder's reading of theming.md, which says brand colours belong to model attributes; the catalog does not state whether runtime branding is possible.
workaround: Decision recorded (see F51 decision).

what: BusinessClock used the JVM zone (CET) while model Timestamp!now() uses the platform zone (UTC), so the return window was an hour off (a 0-day window stayed open). The catalog page on time zones says to use one clock for writing and comparing; the builder wrote the clock before reading it and claimed in R11 that both were UTC.
why: Builder did not consult the platform-behaviour page before writing the custom clock.
workaround: BusinessClock now uses the platform zone (JUDO_PLATFORM_DEFAULT_ZONE_ID, UTC by default); older rows keep the one-hour offset.

what: Timestamp!now() in model expressions follows the platform defaultZoneId (UTC here), while LocalDateTime.now() in custom Java follows the JVM zone; the builder confirmed this against the DB (deliveredAt 05:29 vs UTC 04:29).
why: Two clocks in one platform; the catalog states it and the builder verified it against data.

what: Admin product edits are audited by a post-call interceptor on the built-in update, one AuditEntry per changed field in the same transaction; the bulk price change writes its own rows through an AuditLog service.
why: Built-in update is intercepted and custom operations are not, as the catalog says.

what: Audit log: one row per changed product field (who, what, old and new value), read-only audit page; unchanged fields create no row; bulk price change rows appear too.
why: Built per the F50 row.

what: The builder could not find how to read old and new values in the update interceptor and decompiled the dispatcher jar with javap to learn UpdateInstanceCallPayload, without a kb search.
why: Interceptor payload access is not clear from the interceptor page as the builder read it (unverified); the kb was not searched first.
workaround: Used getInput() and getInstance() from the decompiled class.

what: Order lifecycle integration tests in a hand-written module application/order-tests: 8 tests (new to paid to shipped to delivered with history, refused steps change nothing, return once, stock back, cancel own orders). They found three bugs in ReturnService.
why: Built per the F53 row, in a module outside the generated test kit.
workaround: Hand-written module, see decision.

what: Use a hand-written module (application/order-tests) with the generated pom copied and its i18n-api version filled in, instead of the generated integration-test module.
why: The generated module cannot be read by Maven (empty i18n-api version), and the root fragment override did not win.
workaround: Removed the root fragment after one try; moved the sources to order-tests.

what: The generated application/integration-test/pom.xml declares hu.blackbelt.osgi.i18n:i18n-api with an empty version element, so Maven cannot read the project ('dependencies.dependency.version ... is missing').
why: Template or generator bug in the integration-test pom fragment; the empty element is not filled from a property.
workaround: Hand-written order-tests module with the version filled in.

what: The documented command 'mvn clean test -pl application/integration-test' fails from the project root with 'Could not find the selected project in the reactor', because the module is not in the root reactor. The osgi-ds page says the module is built standalone from its own directory.
why: Catalog command does not match the reactor layout described on the osgi page.
workaround: Ran mvn test from the module directory (later the order-tests module).

what: The testkit has no generated DAO module: the best-practices example uses a project AppDaoModules class that does not exist in the generated project, so the test failed with 'No implementation for ShopConfigDao was bound'. The builder wrote one @Provides per DAO.
why: Catalog example assumes a project DAO module; the generated project does not provide one and the page does not say how to make one.
workaround: Hand-written WebshopDaoModule over ReferenceInjector.

what: The new tests found the builder's own mistakes in ReturnService: an Optional passed to %f, an Optional in the history text, a getProductName call on the wrong object, and a guessed getCode method that is getErrorCode.
why: Builder wrote code against guessed generated APIs.
workaround: Fixed in ReturnService and the test.

what: One integration test failed with 'Outdated instance to update' (IllegalArgumentException in the update DAO processor) after the test changed the product's stock with a stale instance.
why: Probably an instance re-read is needed after an earlier update in the same test; not confirmed against the catalog.

what: Checkout E2E test (two products, address required, order shows cart total) in CI mode: playwright.ci.config.ts with retries and workers from the catalog, headless, waits on responses and on screen only. Passes with CI=true, no retry used.
why: Built per the F54 row.

what: The generated playwright.config.ts sets retries: 4 unconditionally (the template comment says retry on CI only). The catalog's troubleshooting page documents the fix as retries: process.env.CI ? 4 : 0.
why: Generator template ignores the CI condition; catalog already describes the fix.
workaround: Separate playwright.ci.config.ts and playwright.local.config.ts (not generated).

what: 'playwright install chromium' hangs during extraction on this machine, so the local config uses the installed Google Chrome channel.
why: Environment-specific install hang on the builder's machine.
workaround: playwright.local.config.ts with channel chrome and retries 0.

what: judo-cli query esm with --where fqn=... returns nothing, and --select dataType{name} or dataType.name is rejected (scalar fields only), so the builder decompiled and grepped generated code to learn names.
why: CLI query selection rules are not what the builder expected; the catalog page on the CLI was not consulted for query syntax first.
workaround: Used name filters and grep over generated sources.

what: fill creates a menu item for every new access, labelled with the type name (ReturnableItemInfo, ReturnInfo, WishlistInfo). A hand-made MenuItemAccess with a duplicate name fails validation silently or with NamedElementIsUniqueInItsContainer, and move --index did not change the drawer order.
why: Generator creates menu items from access names; CLI menu commands do not change generated order.
workaround: Deleted the extra menu item, relabelled the others, and used the documented menu customizer for order.

what: Menu order of both apps is set by the documented menu customizer hook (customer registerShellHooks MENU_ORDER, admin registerMenuOrder by title), not by model order.
why: Model creation order put Returns to review first and Dashboard last; the hook is the documented route.

what: Enumeration members have no label field (EnumerationMemberUpdateInput has only name, documentation, ordinal), so UI status text must come from a derived string member.
why: Platform input type for enumeration members; the builder read it from the GraphQL input type.
workaround: Derived statusLabel member on ReturnRequest mapped into the screens.

what: After every generate or build the target/judo-cli.jar is deleted, so judo.sh build -i failed with 'Unable to access jarfile' until generate-root was run. Same gap as S01 item 2 (recurring).
why: build-process says build downloads the jar; generate-root and generate delete it.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh generate-root before each CLI call.

what: Each model change cost a stop, generate, build and start cycle of about 3 to 5 minutes (fixed sleeps of 125 to 150 seconds), and the full Playwright runs took about 8 minutes (admin) and 21 minutes (customer).
why: Full redeploy for each model edit and no hot reload used in this round.
workaround: Batched model edits before builds; ran full suites once at the end.

what: The generator writes only application_en-US.json; the Hungarian file is built by a project script (make-hu-translations.py) from the English keys, and new keys must be added to its dictionary each round. The catalog does not say how to keep a second locale file current.
why: Catalog i18n page covers switching, not maintaining a second generated-style locale file.
workaround: Project script scripts/make-hu-translations.py, run after each generate.

what: The test database is kept between runs, so tests broke on accumulated data: Wool socks ran out of stock (restocked by SQL), review, coupon and audit tables grew past one page, FK errors blocked category cleanup, and cleanup errors hid the real failure (a catch was added). F10 and F45 were flaky.
why: Round 12 is the first round that keeps data; earlier rounds wiped the DB and tests assumed an empty one.
workaround: Filter each test to its own stamp, show most rows, restock by SQL, catch cleanup errors; F10 flake fixed at the end.

what: Several Playwright assumptions were wrong: breadcrumb selected by role navigation (MUI breadcrumbs have none), a second Add-to-cart click was ignored while the first call was pending, the dashboard value was read before it loaded, and a price field showed '25.00 EUR' after blur instead of '25'.
why: Tests written against guessed DOM and timing; fixed by class selectors, waiting on responses, and checking the displayed format.
workaround: Changed selectors, awaited the POST response, asserted the displayed value.

what: Frontend build logs show 'XMI ID COLLISION DETECTED' errors for the admin and customer models, but the build still succeeded. The builder did not investigate them.
why: Generator reassigns the same XMI ids to Action objects; cause not checked.
proposed_target: generator: duplicate XMI ids for TabularReferenceField actions

what: kb_get on agent-docs/frontend/advanced-patterns.md returned 'not found', although kb_search had returned that same path.
why: Path mismatch between kb_search hit paths and kb_get lookup (unverified).
workaround: Read the file with grep and ctx_execute instead.

what: Only 18 of 365 tool calls in this chunk were kb calls. The kb guard warned about repeated source searching about 76 times, and the builder kept reading and grepping source. The orchestrator log later records 18 of 365 as well.
why: Standing rule (kb first for every question) was not followed in this round; the builder started with grep and reads.

what: Add-to-message snackbar for operation replies: a documented post-operation hook shows output.message in the snackbar and then calls onSubmit, instead of the generated second dialog.
why: Operations answer with a short ShopMessage; the generated flow opens a second dialog showing it.

what: The builder ran a long series of grep, cat and old-script reads without a kb_search, and the kb guard warned about it about fifteen times in this chunk.
why: Builder reached for session scripts (.scratch/r*.sh), generated sources and grep first, despite the standing kb-first rule.
workaround: Builder kept going on source reads; no kb consult until the guard warnings and later migration steps.

what: CompanyService and ApprovalService did not compile: getCompanyRole, getCompanyAdmin and getPoRequired return plain values, but the builder called orElse on them, then patched with sed.
why: Builder assumed Optional getters for every attribute. The catalog data-access guide says required attributes get plain getters and optional ones get Optional; the builder did not check it before writing code.
workaround: sed edits to ApprovalService and CompanyService to drop orElse; rebuild passed.

what: judo CLI query rejects several field selections: Access target needs a subselection, target{fqn} is not a field, TransferObjectType attributes{...} is not a field, binding needs a subselection, Operation isStatic and ActorType principal{fqn} are not fields.
why: The CLI query schema is not documented in the catalog in a form the builder could use; each guess cost a round trip.
workaround: Builder listed names with grep over fq() output and read the valid-field list printed in each error.
proposed_target: judo CLI query esm (field names and subselection rules)

what: judo query ui MenuItemAccess failed because MenuItemAccess is an esm type, not a ui type; the builder had to fall back to query esm for menu items.
why: Type names for query ui and query esm differ and the CLI error lists valid types without saying which lane holds menus.
workaround: Used query esm MenuItemAccess for the menu list.
proposed_target: judo CLI query ui (type lookup for menu items)

what: Operation buttons and some fields were rejected by update --add feature with the message feature not placeable here, while the same operations existed as UI elements under their own FQN.
why: Unverified: the chunk shows the CLI rule but not the documented route for placing an operation button. The builder did not kb_search this before trying variants.
workaround: Builder updated the generated button element directly by FQN (label, hiddenBy) and did not place it via --add feature.

what: Generated customer frontend fails Biome with a duplicate import: ShopMessage and ShopMessageStored are imported twice when an operation returns a mapped type.
why: Generator emits duplicate imports for a mapped operation output (already recorded as GAPS R8-5, referenced in the checkout hook comment).
workaround: Builder removed the output parameter from the invite operations (-u output), so the generator stopped emitting the import.

what: Build failed with XMI ID COLLISION errors on Admin TabularReferenceField link actions, then ActionContainerSameWithActionDefinition, after new relation-field and action edits.
why: Cause not stated in the chunk. The collision names the Admin TabularReferenceField link actions, and the builder had just added a TabularReferenceField (OrderInfo_Form returns). Not confirmed.
workaround: Builder deleted and re-added table operations and rebuilt; the next build passed after the output change.

what: Frontend Maven step fails at pnpm install with ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS (core-js-pure, esbuild), so the format step fails and the build stops; the same message is in an earlier build log.
why: pnpm blocks dependency build scripts that are not approved; the generated build does not approve them.
workaround: Builder ran npx biome directly instead of pnpm run format.

what: Builder ran biome format and check with --write on the generated customer frontend source, which is generated code.
why: Builder used the formatter as a fix for the pnpm failure instead of approving the build or leaving generated files alone (standing rule: never patch generated files).
workaround: Rebuilt with judo.sh build; build passed at L4750.

what: Running mvn compile in application/app failed in the PSM generator with: there are manual changes in the generated files, discard them or add them to .generator-ignore.
why: Generator checksum guard sees changed generated files. Likely related to c08-09 but not proven in the chunk.
workaround: Builder ran judo.sh generate-root and judo.sh build instead, which passed.

what: discard --force threw away unsaved model edits from a fill run after an error, and the builder had to rebuild those edits.
why: Builder ran fill and an update in one step, then discarded instead of saving first; the edits were not saved.
workaround: Builder re-ran the feature and label edits in later scripts.

what: Invitation key blueprint assumes an anonymous actor, so the invitee cannot accept the key without a Keycloak account. The builder adds sign-up first, then key entry, and shows the key in the admin table and log.
why: Chunk does not show why anonymous acceptance was not used. GAPS R13-3 records the decision as platform limit with no mail server.
workaround: Key shown in the open-invitations table and logged; invitee signs up, then enters key on Join a company; acceptance checks key, expiry and e-mail and deletes the invitation in one transaction.

what: Company members are CustomerAccount rows inside the existing Customer actor (company relation, companyRole BUYER or APPROVER, companyAdmin flag). No third actor.
why: One user has one organization and a small fixed role set, which is the user-with-organization-and-role case. A third actor would add a Keycloak client and a frontend module. B2C must keep working.

what: Model changes went through the F52 migration route: pg_dump before the step, a base model from before the round, a generated migration, a hand-written backfill setting companyAdmin false on existing customers, then execute. No database wipe; 251 customer rows kept.
why: Orchestrator rule for every model change after round 12; a required new flag needs a backfill.

what: Migration command syntax (judo-rdbms-schema:generate and :execute) was recalled from session history with the recall tool instead of kb_search.
why: Builder reached for session memory rather than the catalog schema-evolution guide.
workaround: Used the recalled command; it worked.

what: Generated after-changeset for the new columns and tables contained an unresolved context variable, so the builder rewrote the file by hand and replaced the variable with sed.
why: Unclear from chunk whether the generator is expected to leave this for the developer. The builder states the generator writes the file empty and the backfill is hand-written.
workaround: Hand-written changeset; sed substitution of the context value; execute passed and counts checked by psql.

what: Builder states that the generator adds every new column as a plain nullable column, so an existing row gets NULL and a required flag needs a backfill.
why: Builder read this from the kb (migration-backfill-default-where-null) and applied it.

what: After the build, app start logged NoClassDefFoundError for hu/blackbelt/epsilon/runtime/execution/contexts/EolExecutionContext and Could not find compatible schema model; the same error appears in the round 12 start log.
why: Not resolved in this chunk. Looks like a platform runtime or classpath issue, not a model error.
workaround: Builder kept going; the app answered HTTP 200 on the admin URL.

what: Playwright checks typed 5000 into a number field that shows 5,000, and a Create button matched two elements in a dialog (strict mode).
why: Test design: the test asserted the raw value, not the formatted display; the dialog had two Create buttons.
workaround: Tests now compare the formatted value and use .last() on the dialog Create button.

what: After the buyer joins with the key, the My company menu does not appear until the shell starts again.
why: Builder comment says menu entries are decided from the principal read at shell start, so a page change does not refresh them.
workaround: Post-join hook calls window.location.assign on the start URL to reload the shell.

what: Generated action group shows the first three actions; Request a quote sits under the Actions menu in the cart, so the test must open the menu.
why: Platform behaviour of the generated action group (featured actions), not a bug.
workaround: Test opens Actions and clicks the menu item. Not hidden or patched.

what: Quote lines and company price rows open on their own nested page. Invite a member is enabled only after the company prices are stored with Update.
why: Platform generated edit-page behaviour; Admin.quotes also needed updateable for the discount field.
workaround: Tests open the nested page, edit, Update, Back; Admin.quotes set updateable true.

what: Table pages keep every run's rows and show ten per page, so a test could not find the company or quote it had just created.
why: Test design: the tests relied on the first page of a list that grows with each run.
workaround: Tests filter by name or number with openAddAndApplyFilters.

what: Full customer suite ran with parallel workers: customers shared one cart and one seeded stock, so stock reached zero and tests interfered. Builder reset stock with a direct SQL UPDATE.
why: Test isolation: shared fixtures and parallel workers. Not a code bug.
workaround: Direct SQL reset of stock; new rule: run new spec with --grep @smoke, full suites once, serial.

what: Final full customer suite run was aborted by the tool (Command aborted), so the round's full-suite result is not in this chunk.
why: Cause not shown in the chunk.

what: A sed -i edit to level7.spec.ts replaced a line with the placeholder XX, causing a ReferenceError until fixed.
why: Builder used an unsafe sed pattern on a source file.
workaround: Replaced XX with the intended line in the next step.

what: Several bash commands ran in the same parallel batch as a read of their output, so the read ran first and returned ENOENT.
why: Builder issued bash and read calls without waiting for the write to finish.
workaround: Re-ran the read after the command.

what: Browser snapshot selectors failed on text and role names (Products not found by text or by role name) during admin exploration.
why: Selector and snapshot mismatch in the agent browser tool; not verified further.
workaround: Used snapshot refs and waits instead.

what: About eight full generate and build cycles of two to three minutes each, plus sleeps of up to four minutes, for small label and feature changes.
why: Each label or feature change needs regeneration and build; no faster loop is used in the chunk.
workaround: Batched edits into one rebuild script (rebuild.sh).

what: Money in admin tables and forms (company credit values, quote lines, quote total) uses derived ...Label strings such as '5.00 EUR' instead of the Price component. The numeric fields stay for sums.
why: Same own pattern as round 12 (R12). The orchestrator standing rule asks for the shared Price component in cart, order and card grid, which the builder did use.

what: Companies, members, invitations with key, join by key, company admin invite and role change; the level 7 test for F55 passed.
Company price list with Product.companyPrices; the shared Price component shows the company price, a company without a list sees the list price; the level 7 test passed.
Quantity price tiers (Product.tiers, PriceTierInfo) with unit price switching at 10 and 50; the level 7 test passed.
Checkout branches to PENDING_APPROVAL when the order exceeds the remaining credit; the test passed in the level 7 run with six passing.
Approve and reject operations via ApprovalService; negative test (buyer cannot approve own order) passed in the level 7 run.
Quote and QuoteLine with request a quote from the cart, admin discount and offer, convert to order; the quote test passed after many test fixes.
Purchase order number on SalesOrder and checkout input, required when the company sets poRequired; column added by migration. No separate test result seen in the chunk.
The first E2E run was started with the command timeout, which does not exist on macOS, so the run never started and the shell reported an error.
why: Builder used a GNU coreutils command on a macOS host.
workaround: Started the suite with nohup in the background and polled the log.

what: The full customer E2E suite took 10.6 minutes at 3 workers and the admin suite 2.8 minutes. The user stopped a run as too long and asked for about 5 minutes.
why: Every round ran both full suites; no smoke subset existed.
workaround: Tagged a small @smoke set; each round runs only its new spec plus --grep @smoke; full suites run once at the end of the build.

what: User rule for all later rounds: a round runs its new spec plus --grep @smoke, serially, under about 10 minutes; both full suites run once at the very end.
why: Full-suite runs per round were too slow for the build loop.

what: With 3 workers the tests shared one customer cart and the seeded stock. Running shoe and Trail backpack dropped to 0, so add-to-cart buttons were disabled. Result: 9 customer and 3 admin failures; serial reruns passed.
why: Tests are not isolated; they depend on shared seed data and a database that is kept between runs.
workaround: Serial reruns; stock reset by a direct SQL update to the seed values.

what: The admin order lookup in the F49 test opened the all-orders table and searched the first page only. It broke once the list grew past 10 rows.
why: Test assumed the new order would be on the first page of a table that keeps every run's rows.
workaround: The test now filters the table by order number with openAddAndApplyFilters.

what: The Round 13 report stated that screenshots at 375, 768 and 1440 px existed for F55 to F61, but the builder had viewed only two and had not run ls first. The user found only 2 files.
why: Report written from expectation, not from a directory check.
workaround: Round 14 ran ls per function; a script checks all three widths per name.

what: kb use stayed low. The guard warned many times ('3 consecutive searches without consulting the knowledge base'); the builder kept reading generated code, scratch scripts and jar internals before any kb lookup. Share was 7 of 298 calls in the previous round.
why: Builder habit: go to source first; the kb guard warns but does not stop it.
workaround: None in this chunk; user reminded the builder of the kb-first rule at each round start.

what: Context-mode replaced large bash output with a ctx_search pointer, so the builder had to re-read files or re-run commands to see results.
why: Output above the size limit is indexed and returned as a search pointer instead of raw text.
workaround: Builder switched to the Read tool with offset and limit for the files it needed.

what: The admin quote page showed Requested and Order as editable inputs. The documented read-only options exist only for string fields (textWidget TEXT); date, number and enum fields have no read-only attribute in the catalog.
why: Catalog states read-only for strings only; for other types it points to non-editable mapped or derived members, which the catalog does not show for timestamps.
workaround: Added non-editable copies as mapped members (requestedOn, orderRef, numberText) on Quote and AdminQuoteInfo and labelled them; rebuild succeeded.

what: judo-cli query --select rejects many fields with unhelpful messages: binding and dataType need a subselection that the tool then rejects; readOnly, cardinality, isRowAction and AttributeMember do not exist. Builder needed several calls to find the valid fields.
why: Field names and subselection rules are not discoverable from the CLI help or the catalog.
workaround: Used the valid-field list printed in the error message and grep over JSON output.

what: judo-cli query with --where fqn~= returned nothing, with no error, so the builder's helper showed empty lists for DataMember searches.
why: Operator not supported by the CLI filter or failing silently.
workaround: Builder fell back to listing all DataMembers and grepping by prefix.

what: update --add feature failed for actions containers that do not exist yet ('Container not found', 'element not found'); fill reported 'unchanged'; a row action on a relation table was refused ('refund is not a feature ... placeable here').
why: CLI order of creating the actions group and row actions is not documented; error text does not say what to run first.
workaround: Used the generated refund table operation that already exists on the lines table; the test then opens the action group menu to click it.

what: judo-cli generate printed the line 'ERROR DATABASE HAVE TO BE UPDATED!' and then BUILD SUCCESS, so the level of the message is misleading.
why: Log level of the migration check does not match its meaning.
workaround: Read the message as informational and continued with the migration route.

what: A custom operation with an input and an output (buyGiftCard returning the code) produced a generated dialog that imports the output type twice; the Biome format step failed and the build stopped. Same bug as R8-5.
why: Generator bug with operations that have both input and output; no catalog route recorded.
workaround: buyGiftCard changed to a void operation; the new card shows in My gift cards.

what: The build of the generated e2e model logs many XMI ID COLLISION DETECTED errors for TabularReferenceField link actions; the build still succeeds.
why: Unknown; appears in generated model output.
workaround: None; build passed.

what: New menu entries were labelled with the transfer object name (SellerInfo, SubOrderInfo, WalletInfo, AdminSellerInfo) until translated.
why: Menu label defaults to the transfer object name when a feature is added through the CLI.
workaround: Hungarian translations added for the new labels; the English menu text stayed as the object name at the time of this chunk.

what: The test expected the e-mail as typed, but Keycloak stored and returned it lower-cased.
why: Keycloak lower-cases user names and e-mail addresses; the test did not account for it.
workaround: The test helper lower-cases names and addresses.

what: DAO create on a non-composition two-way relation (customerAccountDao.createPointEntries, createGiftCards) failed with MISSING_REQUIRED_RELATION; only the child DAO create with the back reference works.
why: The kb covers creation through composition parents only; the builder found no note for plain two-way relations.
workaround: pointsEntryDao.create(builder.withCustomer(customer)) and giftCardDao.create(builder.withBuyer(buyer)).

what: A seller who opened the direct page address of another seller's product got the product, its status and an Unpublish button. The access filter hid it from lists only.
why: Derived access filters restrict the generated list queries; a direct identifier GET or update is not filtered. Signed identifiers are not bound to a user.
workaround: SellerOwnershipInterceptor on refresh and update, plus ownership checks inside the custom operations; the page shows a refusal toast and an empty form.

what: The F62 test failed because the other seller's page showed 2 Publish or Unpublish buttons where the test expected 0. The builder changed the assertion to check that the form is empty and the test passed; the reason for the two buttons was not established.
why: Assertion weakened after a failure instead of finding the cause.
workaround: Assertion replaced; later the server-side refusal was added as the real check.

what: Builder guessed a best-practices file name (multi-actor-frontend-architecture.md); the catalog has dual-actor-frontend-architecture.md. kb_get returned not found.
why: File name typed from memory instead of from kb_search output.
workaround: Searched again with kb_search.

what: kb_get returned not found for a section of agent-docs/backend/interceptors.md. The section heading was guessed; the file exists with H1 'Operation Call Interceptors Guide', and the miss does not list the valid section names.
why: Heading guessed from a bracketed kb_search hit; the not-found reply gives no list of sections.
workaround: Builder read the file with grep for headings and then the Read tool.

what: kb_get returned not found for agent-docs/e2e-testing/troubleshooting.md with section 'Speed Up Tests', although the catalog file has that heading at line 430.
why: Possible stale kb index or path mismatch; not confirmed.
workaround: Builder moved on without the section.

what: Integration test imported TransactionHandling from the wrong package and failed to compile. The kb answer (Anti-Pattern 4) was found only after the failure.
why: Import path guessed; kb not consulted first.
workaround: Import changed to fixture.JudoTest.TransactionHandling.

what: Integration test data used SKU 'IT-' plus a number, which fails the Product SKU pattern. 9 of 13 integration tests failed with PATTERN_VALIDATION_FAILED.
why: Test data did not follow the model pattern.
workaround: SKU changed to 'IT-100' plus number; all 13 pass.

what: In the generated checkout dialog, typing the address sometimes sent stray digits to the loyalty points field, and the field's role made fill fail.
why: Builder's guess: the generated dialog loses focus while a debounced text field re-renders.
workaround: resetPoints helper clears and sets the field, waits for the debounce, then checks the value.

what: Admin Exchange rates had no Create button: create -t Access without flags made the access not createable, while the companies access was. The F68 test then timed out waiting for the rate save.
why: Builder did not set createable, updateable and deleteable on the new access; the command default differs by access.
workaround: Set the three flags on Admin.exchangeRates by hand and rebuilt.

what: Rates were returned, but the customer currency switch treated the rate as absent: validOn arrives as a Date object in the generated service, so the string comparison of the day failed.
why: Builder's reading of the generated serializer: dates are turned into Date objects; not documented in the catalog as far as checked.
workaround: Compare calendar days built from the Date object in CurrencySwitch.tsx.

what: The admin clearRates helper stopped after 20 deletes, so rate rows left by earlier runs stayed and the empty-table check failed.
